all.title: Cooking timer that finishes while tab is closed silently loses its History session
all.evidence: js/cooking-ui.js:74-108 cookingTimerAlarm() is the ONLY site that calls History.addSession({type:'cooking'}). It is wired solely via timer.onAlarm() (line 34/60), which fires from Timer.checkFinished() → alarmCallback (js/timer.js:112-115). But Timer.loadState (js/timer.js:154-171, non-overshoot branch) sets status='finished'+alarmFired=true WITHOUT invoking alarmCallback. So a cook timer that crossed zero while the tab was closed reloads as 'finished' and never logs to history. RUNTIME-VERIFY: start a 1-min cook timer, close the tab, reopen after 90s — the timer shows Done but no 'cooking' session appears in History/Analytics.
all.rootCause: addSession is coupled to the live alarm callback, which loadState's recovery path deliberately suppresses to avoid re-chiming. Flow handles this exact case (js/flow-ui.js:361-363 re-saves on overflowing restore); Cooking has no equivalent.
all.proposedFix: In initCookingUI() (after loadCookingTimers), for each timer whose restored status is 'finished' and whose duration>0, log the missed cooking session to History once (guard with a per-timer 'logged' flag persisted in the saved record, e.g. ct.loggedAt, to stay idempotent across reopens). Reuse History.addSession and the existing record shape.

all.title: Timer / Interval / Sequence missed-completion on reload never fires the alarm/history side effects
all.evidence: Engine loadState recovery branches set alarmFired=true and the terminal/overflowing status but do NOT invoke the phase/alarm callbacks: js/timer.js:154-171, js/interval.js:278-298, js/sequence.js:142-146. For Timer the alarm (chime/haptic/notify in js/timer-ui.js:232-239) is skipped on reopen — acceptable. But the SESSION isn't lost for Timer because onTimerLeft logs from the Reset/Done button (js/timer-ui.js:60-68). Interval terminal-on-reload (js/interval.js:285-292) → overflowing → onIntervalRight/Left logs on user Reset, so OK. Sequence loadState (js/sequence.js:142-146) lands in 'phaseComplete' but the auto-advance/history-on-done logic lives only in the Sequence.onPhaseComplete callback (js/sequence-ui.js:17-38), which is NEVER re-fired on reload — a multi-phase Sequence that completed its final phase while closed will reopen stuck at 'phaseComplete' on a mid-phase, and the final 'done' history write can be skipped. RUNTIME-VERIFY: run a 2-phase Sequence, close during phase 1's final seconds, reopen — observe whether it auto-advances and whether the 'sequence' history row is written.
all.rootCause: Phase-advance + history-write side effects live in UI callbacks that only run from the live RAF tick, while loadState recovery is silent by design.
all.proposedFix: In initSequenceUI after loadState, if status==='phaseComplete' call Sequence.advancePhase()+restart (or surface a resume affordance) so the chain isn't stuck; mirror the Interval auto-advance restore. Keep the chime suppressed but ensure the terminal 'done' history write path can run on reopen.

all.title: Stale 'focusComplete' status string in app.js leaves a dead progress-bar branch
all.evidence: js/app.js:217 checks `Flow.getStatus() === 'focusComplete'` to hide the progress bar, but the Flow engine renamed that status to 'overflowing' (js/flow.js:7-11, migration at js/flow.js:262). 'focusComplete' is now unreachable from getStatus(), so the intended 'hide progress bar during focus-overflow' never triggers — during focus overflow the bar stays visible (Flow's own updateFlowUI at js/flow-ui.js:601-606 governs it, but applyAppMode runs on mode-switch and would show a full bar). focus-ui.js:158 has the same dead 'phaseComplete' branch for Flow/Pomodoro (those engines no longer emit it either).
all.rootCause: Engine state-machine rename (focusComplete→overflowing, several →overflowing) was not propagated to two consumer call sites.
all.proposedFix: In js/app.js:217 replace 'focusComplete' with 'overflowing' (and add 'recoveryOverflowing' if the bar should hide there too). Audit focus-ui.js:158 status labels against the current engine status sets.

all.title: Cooking alarm tone/notification bound to a stale array index after deletion
all.evidence: js/cooking-ui.js:34 and :60 capture `idx` in the onAlarm closure (`() => cookingTimerAlarm(timer, idx)`). On load, idx is the load-loop index; in addCookingTimer it's cookingTimers.length at creation. removeCookingTimer (js/cooking-ui.js:66-72) splices the array WITHOUT re-binding remaining timers' alarms, so after deleting a middle timer every later timer's alarm uses a wrong idx → wrong COOKING_TONES frequency (js/cooking-ui.js:6,76). Not data corruption (idx only selects tone via modulo), but the audible cue no longer matches the slot.
all.rootCause: Index captured by value at bind time; the array is mutable and indices shift on delete.
all.proposedFix: Pass `ct.id` (stable) instead of idx and derive the tone from the timer's current position via cookingTimers.findIndex(c=>c.id===id) at alarm time, or store the tone on the ct record at creation.

all.title: Stopwatch history saver can drop laps/elapsed on a fast pause→reset between 500ms ticks
all.evidence: js/app.js:489-512 polls every 500ms to detect a stopwatch transitioning to 'idle' and then writes History.addSession with the LAST-CAPTURED prev.elapsed/prev.laps. prev is only refreshed when status!=='idle' (lines 496-499). If a user pauses then resets (idle) and starts a new run all within one 500ms window, the poll sees status==='running' (or idle) with a stale or zeroed snapshot, so the just-finished session's elapsed/laps can be lost or under-recorded. Also onLeftClick reset (js/ui.js:88-96) does NOT itself write history — it relies entirely on this poll, so any missed transition = lost session.
all.rootCause: Session-on-reset detection is sampled by a coarse 500ms interval reading derived state, instead of being captured synchronously at the reset gesture.
all.proposedFix: Capture and write the session synchronously in UI.onLeftClick at the paused→reset branch (it already snapshots lastResetState at js/ui.js:88) — write History.addSession there with the pre-reset elapsed+laps, and keep the poll only as a backstop for tab-close. Guard against double-write with the existing lastKnownStates map.

all.title: Pomodoro 'overflowing' Skip vs Break both call nextPhase but onPomodoroLeft (Skip) never re-starts the next phase
all.evidence: On overflowing, onPomodoroRight (js/pomodoro-ui.js:305-339) calls nextPhase() then Pomodoro.start() so the next phase begins running. But onPomodoroLeft 'Skip' (js/pomodoro-ui.js:263-269) calls nextPhase() and saves WITHOUT start() — leaving the engine in 'idle' on the next phase. The button labels (js/pomodoro-ui.js:475-485) present BOTH as actions ('Skip' left, 'Break'/'Work' right) during overflow, so 'Skip' silently lands the user in a paused-looking idle next phase requiring an extra Start tap, while 'Break/Work' auto-runs. Inconsistent; also if longBreak overflows, Skip→nextPhase sets status='done' (js/pomodoro.js:188-194) which is the intended terminal, but the session is NOT written to history on the Skip path (only onPomodoroRight's done branch at :310-325 writes it).
all.rootCause: Two overflow-advance entry points (left=Skip, right=Break/Work) diverge: only the right path starts the next phase and only the right path writes the done-session to history.
all.proposedFix: Either make Skip also call start() for parity, or relabel so only one control advances. Critically, ensure the longBreak→done transition writes the History.addSession regardless of whether the user reached 'done' via Skip (left) or Break/Work (right).

all.title: Interval auto-advance restart fires BgNotify + start() inside the phase-complete callback without re-checking appMode
all.evidence: js/interval-ui.js:14-33 onPhaseComplete handler unconditionally calls Interval.advancePhase()+Interval.start()+startIntervalRenderLoop() for type phase/rest/roundEnd. checkFinished only runs from the RAF tick (js/interval-ui.js:391) which is appMode-guarded, so this is mostly safe. But if the user switches modes exactly as a phase completes, the callback still restarts the engine and reschedules a BgNotify for a mode the user left, and startIntervalRenderLoop's tick will no-op-return on the appMode check — leaving the engine 'running' with a scheduled notification but no UI loop until the user returns. RUNTIME-VERIFY: switch away from Interval at the instant a Tabata phase ends; check that a stray 'Interval' notification doesn't fire and the engine state is consistent on return.
all.rootCause: Phase-complete side effects (start + notify) are not guarded by the current appMode the way the render loop is.
all.proposedFix: Guard the auto-advance block in onPhaseComplete with `if (appMode === 'interval')` (consistent with every other handler) and skip the BgNotify reschedule when not the active mode.

all.title: Pomodoro revertPhase folds current break elapsed into the restored work phase (time-travel artifact)
all.evidence: js/pomodoro.js:200-214 revertPhase restores phase/cycleIndex from the snapshot but sets accumulatedMs = snapshot.accumulatedMs + currentElapsed, where currentElapsed is the time already spent in the NEW (break) phase. So if the user ran 4 min into a short break and taps '← Go back', they resume the previous WORK phase already 4 min advanced beyond where it was snapshotted. Combined with the snapshot capturing accumulatedMs at the moment of nextPhase (which for an overflowed phase is the full duration), the restored work phase can immediately read as complete/overflowing.
all.rootCause: currentElapsed (break-phase time) is added to a work-phase accumulator; the two phases have different durations so the carry is semantically wrong.
all.proposedFix: Decide the intended semantics: most natural is to restore the previous phase to exactly its snapshot state (drop the currentElapsed carry, or start it fresh/paused). At minimum clamp so the restored phase can't instantly exceed its own duration.

all.title: Cooking timer adjust (+3/−3) and quick-set can't extend a finished timer; no re-arm path
all.evidence: Timer.setDuration is gated on status==='idle' (js/timer.js:22-25) and adjustRemainingMs only works in running/paused (js/timer.js:27-28). A finished cook timer (status==='finished') exposes only Reset (js/cooking-ui.js:144-147), which zeroes duration. There's no '+N min to keep going' on a finished cook timer — the user must Reset then re-pick a quick time. Minor, but the per-card +3/−3 row is hidden for finished (js/cooking-ui.js:149) so the affordance is simply absent. Acceptable by design but worth flagging as an interaction dead-end.
all.rootCause: Cook timers use the non-overshoot Timer (halt-at-zero) so 'finished' is terminal; the UI offers no extend-from-finished.
all.proposedFix: Optional: on 'finished', offer a '+1m / +5m' that resets the timer to that duration and auto-starts (effectively a quick re-arm), or document this as intended.

all.title: Multiple cooking timers finishing in the same RAF frame each open a new AudioContext and double-log
all.evidence: startCookingRenderLoop (js/cooking-ui.js:267-296) iterates all timers and calls checkFinished() on each per frame. cookingTimerAlarm (js/cooking-ui.js:74-108) constructs a fresh `new AudioContext()` per alarm (line 79) and calls History.addSession + saveCookingTimers + renderCookingTimers. If several timers cross zero in the same tick, multiple AudioContexts are created (browsers cap ~6 and then throw, caught silently) and renderCookingTimers runs N times in one frame. Functionally tolerable but wasteful and can drop later chimes once the AudioContext cap is hit.
all.rootCause: Per-alarm AudioContext allocation instead of a shared/pooled context; no batching of the render after multiple simultaneous completions.
all.proposedFix: Reuse a single module-level AudioContext (lazily created, resumed on user gesture) for cook chimes, and collapse the post-completion render to once per frame.

all.title: Stopwatch deleteLap can desync lapStartMs when deleting the most-recent completed lap while running
all.evidence: js/stopwatch.js:51-60 deleteLap recomputes lapStartMs from the remaining tail (laps[last].totalMs) or offsetMs when empty. But the in-progress current lap's elapsed is derived as getElapsedMs()-lapStartMs (js/stopwatch.js:75-78). If the user swipe-deletes the latest completed lap WHILE running (swipe handlers are attached to completed laps and Persistence.save runs, js/ui.js:330-343), lapStartMs jumps back to the prior lap's total, so the current in-progress lap suddenly shows a much larger time (it now spans the deleted lap's interval too). RUNTIME-VERIFY: run stopwatch, record 3 laps, keep running, swipe-delete lap 3 — observe the current lap time jump.
all.rootCause: deleteLap rebases lapStartMs to the new tail, but the running current-lap measurement assumes lapStartMs marks where the live lap began, not where the deleted lap began.
all.proposedFix: When deleting the most-recent completed lap while status==='running', leave lapStartMs at its current value (don't rebase to the prior lap), or recompute so the live lap's start is preserved. Only rebase for deletions of non-tail laps or when paused.

all.title: createTimer default-id collision: addStopwatch/addTimer use Date.now().toString(36) which can collide on rapid add
all.evidence: js/instance-manager.js:14 ('sw-'+Date.now().toString(36)) and :47 ('tm-'+...) plus js/cooking-ui.js:55 (id=Date.now().toString(36)) derive ids from Date.now() alone. Two adds within the same millisecond (e.g. a fast double-tap on Add, or programmatic add) produce identical ids. For stopwatches/timers MAX_INSTANCES=5 makes this rare; for cooking (≤8) the id is also used as the BgNotify key ('cook-'+id, js/cooking-ui.js:193) and the React-less key in render — a collision means two cards share a BgNotify channel and delete-by-id removes both. Meds avoid this by appending Math.random (js/meds.js:500).
all.rootCause: Time-only id generation without a random/counter suffix, unlike the meds id scheme.
all.proposedFix: Append a short random suffix or an incrementing counter to the add-time ids (mirror js/meds.js:500 '+Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,5)').

all.title: Pomodoro/Flow render loop self-heals on visibility but Interval/Timer/Cooking/Sequence do not restart their RAF on tab refocus
all.evidence: js/ui.js:20-29 visibilitychange restarts the stopwatch and pomodoro render loops on becoming visible. There is no equivalent for Timer (timerRafId), Interval (intervalRafId), Cooking (cookingRafId), Flow (flowRafId), or Sequence (sequenceRafId). When a tab is backgrounded, RAF is throttled/paused; on the SAME tab, the loop's last scheduled frame eventually resumes, so the model self-corrects via wall-clock derivation (this is fine — the drift-free model holds). But if the loop had ALREADY exited (e.g. a paused→started transition while hidden, or after a checkFinished set status) the display can be stale until a user interaction. RUNTIME-VERIFY: start a Timer, background the tab for 2 min, foreground — confirm the display catches up immediately rather than only after a click. The drift model is correct; this is purely a loop-resume gap, do NOT alter the timing formula.
all.rootCause: The visibilitychange handler only re-arms stopwatch + pomodoro loops; the other modes rely on their loop never having stopped.
all.proposedFix: Extend the existing visibilitychange handler (js/ui.js:20-29) to re-call the active mode's startXxxRenderLoop when the corresponding engine is in a ticking status and appMode matches. Keep the wall-clock formula untouched — this only re-arms RAF.

all.title: loadState clock-skew guard fixes future startedAt but not future accumulatedMs / corrupt durations
all.evidence: Every loadState guards `startedAt > Date.now()` (e.g. js/stopwatch.js:140-143, js/timer.js:149-152, js/pomodoro.js:292-295, js/flow.js:283-286, js/interval.js:274-277, js/sequence.js:138-141). None validate that accumulatedMs / durationMs / offsetMs are finite non-negative numbers — a hand-edited or corrupt localStorage blob with accumulatedMs:'foo' or durationMs:-5 flows straight into the arithmetic. JSON.parse failures ARE caught and the key removed (app.js:14-17,23-26; instance-manager.js:102-104), so the risk is a structurally-valid-but-semantically-bad record. getElapsedMs uses Math.max(0,…) for stopwatch (js/stopwatch.js:17) which absorbs negatives, but Timer/Pomodoro overshoot math has no such floor on accumulatedMs.
all.rootCause: Field-level type/range validation is absent in loadState; only top-level JSON.parse and a single future-timestamp check exist.
all.proposedFix: Add a small sanitizer in each loadState: coerce accumulatedMs/durationMs/offsetMs/phaseAdjustmentMs via `Number()` and clamp non-finite/negative to 0 before use. Reuse a shared helper to avoid drift across engines.

all.title: Meds getDosesToday uses local-midnight cutoff but offset-logged doses crossing midnight are mis-bucketed vs supply derivation
all.evidence: getDosesToday (js/meds.js:278-286) counts doseLog entries with takenAt >= local startOfToday(). 'Took it ~X ago' logs a backdated takenAt (js/meds.js:229-242). If a user near midnight logs a dose '~40 min ago' that lands before midnight, it correctly drops out of 'today' — consistent. But consumedSinceReset (js/meds.js:290-297) counts doses >= supplyResetAt regardless of day, and getStatusToday (js/meds.js:317-326) compares takenToday to expected. The walk-from-tail-and-break logic in both getDosesToday and consumedSinceReset ASSUMES strict ascending sort and that all 'today' entries are contiguous at the tail — true after logDose's sort (js/meds.js:238), but a backdated dose inserted mid-array then a forward dose means the tail-break in getDosesToday could stop early if an older-than-today dose sits between two today doses. Sort prevents this in practice, but the break-on-first-older assumption is fragile if any code path appends without re-sorting.
all.rootCause: getDosesToday/consumedSinceReset short-circuit on the first out-of-window entry, relying on a sort invariant maintained only by logDose; any future append-without-sort breaks the count silently.
all.proposedFix: Replace the break-early loops with a full filter+count (cheap at ≤1000 entries) so correctness no longer depends on the contiguity assumption, or assert the sort invariant. Low risk; meds counts feed the supply badge + status.

all.title: Flow saveFlowSessionToHistory re-save on advance can double-count overshoot=0 then overwrite, but reset-before-save races lose late overshoot
all.evidence: saveFlowSessionToHistory (js/flow-ui.js:1088-1139) is intentionally idempotent via id=sessionStartedAt (IDB put). It is called at focus-complete (js/flow-ui.js:186-188), again on Start Recovery (js/flow-ui.js:313) and Skip Recovery (js/flow-ui.js:331). overshootMs is captured only when isOvershooting()&&phase==='focus' (js/flow-ui.js:1108-1111). On the recoveryOverflowing→End path (js/flow-ui.js:468-484) and the recovery skip path, saveFlowSessionToHistory is NOT re-called, so recovery-phase overshoot is never recorded (acknowledged in the comment at :469-471). Also endFocusEarly (js/flow.js:144-159) sets status='overflowing' with focusEndedAt=now but accumulatedMs holds real elapsed — the summary's endedEarly fudge (js/flow-ui.js:1022 uses 5s, but the history record at :1097 uses a strict `<plannedMs` with no fudge), so a naturally-completed block whose elapsed is plannedMs-1ms due to float rounding could be flagged endedEarly in history but not in the summary. RUNTIME-VERIFY: complete a 90-min block naturally and confirm session.endedEarly is absent.
all.rootCause: Two different endedEarly thresholds (5s fudge in summary vs exact compare in the history write) and recovery-overshoot intentionally unrecorded.
all.proposedFix: Align the history-record endedEarly compare with the summary's 5s fudge (js/flow-ui.js:1097 use `elapsedMs < plannedMs - 5000`). Decide whether recovery overshoot should be persisted; if not, leave the documented gap.

all.title: Pomodoro render loop rebuilds the entire phase timeline + dots via innerHTML every RAF frame (~60×/sec)
all.evidence: js/pomodoro-ui.js:528-548 startPomodoroRenderLoop() calls updatePomodoroUI() every requestAnimationFrame. updatePomodoroUI() (js/pomodoro-ui.js:391 renderPomodoroDots(); :397 renderPomodoroTimeline()) runs unconditionally each frame. renderPomodoroDots (js/pomodoro-ui.js:501-526) does dotsEl.innerHTML = html each call; renderPomodoroTimeline (js/pomodoro-ui.js:1308-1406) rebuilds the whole bar via el.innerHTML AND calls loadChecklist() (js/pomodoro-ui.js:571-575 → JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(...))) + endTime.toLocaleTimeString (js/pomodoro-ui.js:1377) every frame. RUNTIME-VERIFY: open DevTools Performance, run a Pomodoro, confirm ~60 innerHTML rebuilds/sec + 60 localStorage reads/sec on the timeline element.
all.rootCause: The RAF tick reuses the full mode-render function (designed for discrete state transitions) as the per-frame painter. Only the time digits + progress bar change each frame; the dots, timeline, phase labels, cycle label, button HTML, and checklist visibility are state-derived and change only on phase transitions.
all.proposedFix: Split updatePomodoroUI into a cheap per-frame painter (time innerHTML + progress-bar width + overshoot class) and a structural updater (dots, timeline, buttons, labels). Call only the painter from the RAF tick; call the structural updater from onPomodoroLeft/Right/onPhaseComplete/configure. Mirror the Stopwatch updateCurrentLap pattern. Cache loadChecklist() result outside the frame loop. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump required.

all.title: Flow render loop calls full updateFlowUI() (innerHTML, multiple renderFlowUserTasks, applyFlowReadinessSuggestion) every RAF frame
all.evidence: js/flow-ui.js:1141-1179 startFlowRenderLoop tick() calls updateFlowUI() every frame. updateFlowUI (js/flow-ui.js:505) sets timeEl.innerHTML, toggles ~6 classes, and during isFocusActive calls renderFlowUserTasks() (js/flow-ui.js:570) which does container.innerHTML on TWO targets + re-attaches change/click listeners to every task row, plus updateFlowUserTaskCount() — all per frame. renderFlowUserTasks (js/flow-ui.js:731-789) loops both 'flow-user-tasks-items' and 'flow-running-tasks-items' rebuilding innerHTML and re-binding listeners. RUNTIME-VERIFY: start a Flow block with 3+ tasks, confirm task-list innerHTML rebuilds + listener re-binds 60×/sec.
all.rootCause: Same anti-pattern as Pomodoro: the per-frame loop reuses the structural render function. renderFlowUserTasks re-binding listeners on every frame also creates GC churn and risks duplicate handlers if a row node is ever reused.
all.proposedFix: Restrict the per-frame work to time + progress fill. Move renderFlowUserTasks() out of updateFlowUI's hot path — call it only on task mutations and on phase entry (it's already idempotent from storage). Same painter/structural split as Pomodoro. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Timer & Interval render loops rebuild all button innerHTML + toggle classes every RAF frame
all.evidence: js/timer-ui.js:201-219 startTimerRenderLoop calls updateTimerUI() each frame; updateTimerUI (js/timer-ui.js:101) sets btnLeft.innerHTML + btnRight.innerHTML in the switch (lines 157-196) and toggles classes every frame even though button state only changes on transitions. js/interval-ui.js:385-404 startIntervalRenderLoop → updateIntervalUI() each frame; updateIntervalUI (js/interval-ui.js:269) sets phaseLabel.textContent/.style.color, nextLabel, roundLabel, and button innerHTML (lines 348-380) every frame.
all.rootCause: Per-frame loop reuses the structural render. Writing identical innerHTML/className every frame forces the browser to re-parse button markup and recompute style even when nothing changed.
all.proposedFix: Painter/structural split as above: per-frame writes only time innerHTML + progress width (+ overshoot/finished class which is time-derived). Button HTML and phase labels move to transition-driven calls. Low risk because the values are deterministic from status. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Always-on 500ms setInterval in app.js polls every stopwatch instance for the app's entire lifetime
all.evidence: js/app.js:489-512 setInterval(...,500) runs forever (never cleared, no visibility/mode guard). Each tick iterates InstanceManager.getStopwatches(), calls getElapsedMs() + getLaps() on each, and maintains lastKnownStates Map. It fires even when the user is in Rhythm/Wellness/Pomodoro/Flow with no stopwatch running, and even when document.hidden.
all.rootCause: Session-on-reset detection was implemented as a global poller instead of hooking the stopwatch reset path (onLeftClick already handles reset). getLaps() may return a fresh array each call (allocation) twice per second indefinitely.
all.proposedFix: Replace the poller with an event-driven save: stopwatch reset already flows through UI.onLeftClick / Stopwatch.reset — capture the pre-reset state there and write History.addSession, dropping the interval entirely. If a poller must stay, gate it on document.visibilityState==='visible' && appMode==='stopwatch' && at least one instance non-idle, and clear it otherwise. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: lastKnownStates Map in app.js grows without eviction when instances are deleted
all.evidence: js/app.js:487 const lastKnownStates = new Map(); only ever .set (js/app.js:510) inside the 500ms poller; there is no .delete when InstanceManager.removeStopwatch (js/instance-manager.js:21) drops an instance. Each entry also retains a laps[] array reference (js/app.js:497-499).
all.rootCause: The poller keys by instance id but never reconciles against the live instance set, so deleted-instance entries (and their retained laps arrays) leak for the session.
all.proposedFix: If the poller is kept, prune lastKnownStates to current instance ids each tick (or delete on removeStopwatch). Best resolved by removing the poller entirely (see prior finding). sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: meds-ui 30s ticker is started at init and never stopped (no stopTick); runs for app lifetime
all.evidence: js/meds-ui.js:452-457 startTick() sets a 30s setInterval calling refreshAllCards() (js/meds-ui.js:200-202 → MedsManager.all().forEach(refreshCardStatus)); grep confirms zero stopTick and zero clearInterval in meds-ui.js. The interval body guards on isSurfaceVisible() (js/meds-ui.js:459-464) so it no-ops work when hidden, but the timer itself never clears and the visibility check runs forever.
all.rootCause: Ticker lifecycle is fire-and-forget at init rather than tied to surface activation/deactivation.
all.proposedFix: Pair startTick with a stopTick(clearInterval) and call it when the Meds surface deactivates (TempoNav pillar/sub change), or start it lazily on first activation. Low impact (30s cadence, guarded body) but it's a real never-cleared timer. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: renderLaps does a full lap-list innerHTML rebuild + re-attaches all swipe handlers on every lap event
all.evidence: js/ui.js:179-249 renderLaps() builds the entire list string and assigns lapList.innerHTML = html (js/ui.js:232), then calls renderLapStats(), renderLapChart() (full SVG innerHTML, js/ui.js:251-283), and attachSwipeHandlers() (js/ui.js:285-349) which adds 3 touch listeners PER lap row. It's invoked on every Stopwatch.lap() via onLeftClick (js/ui.js:86 renderLaps(true)). At N laps this rebuilds N rows + binds 3N listeners per lap press. (CLAUDE.md already flags this.)
all.rootCause: Lap recording rebuilds the whole list instead of prepending the one new row; swipe handlers are bound per-row instead of via one delegated listener on lapList.
all.proposedFix: Prepend only the new completed-lap row (and update the current-lap row) on lap; rebuild fully only on display-mode toggle/delete/load. Replace per-row touch listeners with a single delegated touchstart/move/end on lapList using e.target.closest('.lap-swipeable'). Also rebuild the chart only when it's visible/changed. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: 80 render-blocking serial <script> tags with no defer/async inflate TTI on cold load
all.evidence: index.html lines 1108-1232 list 80 <script src> tags (grep -c '<script' = 80) and grep for defer/async on script tags returns nothing. Each is parser-blocking and fetched/executed in series. On a cold (uncached) load every module blocks HTML parsing and first paint sequentially.
all.rootCause: The load-order-as-dependency-graph design relies on synchronous global side effects at script eval time, which precludes module bundling but does NOT preclude defer (defer preserves document order while unblocking the parser).
all.proposedFix: Add the defer attribute to every <script> tag (defer guarantees in-order execution after HTML parse, matching the current dependency contract) — single mechanical change, no code restructure, no bundler. Verify nothing reads the DOM before DOMContentLoaded (app.js init runs at end so it's fine). This is the cheapest TTI win that stays vanilla. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump (index.html changed).

all.title: CardsUI status-dot className recomputed for every non-primary card on a 100ms interval
all.evidence: js/cards-ui.js:169-216 startCardTick() runs setInterval(updateCardTimes, 100). updateCardTimes (js/cards-ui.js:181-216) per tick does container.querySelector for each instance's time el AND each card, then unconditionally rebuilds dot.className from status (js/cards-ui.js:204-210) even when status is unchanged. Two querySelectors per instance per 100ms.
all.rootCause: No memoization of last-rendered status/time; className string rebuilt every tick. Also uses a 100ms interval rather than RAF (less smooth, but fires when hidden too — no visibility guard).
all.proposedFix: Cache last status per instance id and only write className/textContent on change; cache the el references from render() instead of re-querying each tick; optionally switch to RAF with a visibility guard. Low impact (capped at 5 instances) but it's needless per-tick work. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Cooking mode creates a brand-new AudioContext on every timer alarm (never closed)
all.evidence: js/cooking-ui.js:74-108 cookingTimerAlarm() does new (window.AudioContext||webkitAudioContext)() per alarm (js/cooking-ui.js:79) and never calls ctx.close(). The shared SFX module already owns a single reusable AudioContext (js/audio.js:33-38 getCtx()) and a beep() helper (js/audio.js:50-65). Browsers cap concurrent AudioContexts (~6 in Chrome); repeated cooking alarms can exhaust them and start throwing.
all.rootCause: Cooking implements its own per-alarm oscillator instead of reusing SFX.getCtx/beep, leaking an AudioContext each time and reimplementing existing functionality.
all.proposedFix: Route cooking alarm tones through the shared SFX context (add a parameterized SFX.beep call or a small SFX.playTone(freq) using getCtx()), eliminating the per-alarm AudioContext. Reuse-over-reimplementation. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Pomodoro RAF tick re-reads checklist from localStorage + calls toLocaleTimeString every frame
all.evidence: Inside the per-frame renderPomodoroTimeline (reached from updatePomodoroUI in the RAF loop), js/pomodoro-ui.js:1370 const goals = loadChecklist() performs JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('pomodoro_checklist')) (js/pomodoro-ui.js:571-575); js/pomodoro-ui.js:1377 endStr = endTime.toLocaleTimeString(...) (Intl formatting is comparatively expensive); both execute ~60×/sec for the whole session.
all.rootCause: Synchronous storage read + JSON parse + Intl format placed on the hottest path. localStorage.getItem is a synchronous main-thread call; doing it 60×/sec is wasteful and can contend with other storage writes (Persistence.save).
all.proposedFix: Subsumed by the Pomodoro painter/structural split (timeline only needs rebuilding on config/phase change, not per frame). If the timeline must update mid-frame, cache the parsed checklist and the formatted end-time string and recompute only on transition. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Rhythm Insights renders all 9 panels into one large innerHTML string with no incremental/virtualized paint
all.evidence: js/rhythm-insights.js:397-468 renderInto() builds html by concatenating every registered panel's render() output (each panel is 90-300 lines of SVG/HTML string: bfrb-triggers 298, meds-sleep 239, recovery-trends 161, etc.) then assigns container.innerHTML once (js/rhythm-insights.js:438). On every route to Insights AND on every panel toggle (js/rhythm-insights.js:449 re-runs full renderInto) it rebuilds ALL panels, not just the toggled one.
all.rootCause: Single-shot full-board rebuild is simple and isolation-safe (Promise.allSettled), but a panel toggle (e.g. Onset/Duration on meds-sleep) re-builds and re-paints all 9 panels including re-running their async build() (History/Analytics reads).
all.proposedFix: On a data-insight-action toggle, re-render only the affected panel's <section> (replace that node's outerHTML) instead of the whole container; keep the full rebuild for route-in. Memoize the per-render memoized getSessions already exists (js/rhythm-insights.js:409-412) — extend that caching across a toggle so build() isn't re-paying IDB reads. Low impact (Insights is not a hot loop) but avoids a visible full-board flash on toggle. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: applyAppMode performs ~25 individual getElementById + classList.toggle layout-affecting writes per mode switch
all.evidence: js/app.js:185-254 applyAppMode() does ~25 sequential document.getElementById(...).classList.toggle('hidden', ...) calls (js/app.js:202-227) interleaved with reads of engine status, then calls CardsUI.render() + the active mode's update. Each .hidden toggle can invalidate layout; doing 25 in sequence with interleaved status reads risks layout thrash.
all.rootCause: Visibility orchestration is a flat list of element toggles rather than a class on a parent (e.g. body[data-mode]) that CSS resolves in one pass.
all.proposedFix: Set a single data-mode attribute on a container and drive section visibility via CSS selectors ([data-mode='pomodoro'] #pomodoro-area {display:...}), collapsing 25 JS writes + reflows into one attribute write. Larger CSS change; lower priority since it fires only on user mode switch, not per frame. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump (css + js).

all.title: Service worker fetch handler is cache-first with no runtime update path for navigations
all.evidence: sw.js:110-133 fetch handler returns caches.match(...) || fetch(...) (cache-first, no stale-while-revalidate, no network-first for navigations). Combined with skipWaiting()+clients.claim() (sw.js:96,107) and a manual CACHE_NAME bump per deploy (sw.js:1), users get fresh content only after a version bump + the next two loads. The repo's own memory notes 'kapture serves stale SW-cached JS'.
all.rootCause: Pure cache-first is fast but means any missed CACHE_NAME bump (a frequent footgun noted in CLAUDE.md) silently serves stale code, and there's no background revalidation to self-heal.
all.proposedFix: Keep cache-first for static assets but add stale-while-revalidate (return cache, fetch in background, update cache) so a missed bump self-corrects on next load; OR network-first for the navigation request (index.html) only. This improves freshness/TTI tradeoff without abandoning offline. FROZEN-sync note: this is sw.js, not the Firestore sync layer, so it's in scope. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Compare-view RAF loop runs even when neither instance is being viewed if exit path is missed; re-binds handlers on every button press via full renderCompare
all.evidence: js/compare-ui.js:116-177 attachCompareHandlers binds blur/keydown/click listeners; every control press calls renderCompare() (js/compare-ui.js:151,173) which does view.innerHTML = ... (js/compare-ui.js:64) then re-runs attachCompareHandlers — full rebuild + re-bind per button tap. The per-frame loop (js/compare-ui.js:180-213) correctly updates only the time nodes, which is good, but the button-press path rebuilds the whole view.
all.rootCause: State changes trigger a full innerHTML rebuild + listener re-bind rather than targeted updates; acceptable at 2 columns but inconsistent with the efficient time-node-only RAF path right beside it.
all.proposedFix: On a control press, update only the affected column's button labels/classes and let the RAF loop keep painting the time; avoid the full renderCompare()+re-bind. Or delegate the two button handlers once. Minor — 2 columns only. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: updateDisplay calls Analog.update() every frame even when the analog face is hidden (digital mode)
all.evidence: js/ui.js:135-143 updateDisplay() unconditionally calls Analog.update(ms) every frame. Analog.update (js/analog.js:82-101) early-returns when mode!=='analog' (js/analog.js:83), so the cost is just a function call + Date math guard — but updateDisplay also always sets timeEl.innerHTML with a <span> child (js/ui.js:138/140) rather than updating text nodes, re-parsing the centiseconds span markup every frame.
all.rootCause: Per-frame innerHTML (with an inner <span>) forces HTML parse each tick; the structure is constant and only the digit text changes.
all.proposedFix: Build the time + centiseconds span once and update only the two text nodes (timeMain.textContent / centi.textContent) on subsequent frames, avoiding innerHTML re-parse 60×/sec. Same micro-pattern can apply to timer/pomodoro/flow/interval time displays. Low individual impact but multiplied across all modes' hot paths. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump.

all.title: Global BFRB renderLabel runs on every window focus + hashchange; commitPending bound to 3 navigation events
all.evidence: js/global-bfrb.js:414-415 renderLabel is bound to both window 'hashchange' and 'focus'; js/global-bfrb.js:427-429 commitPending bound to pagehide, beforeunload, AND hashchange. Every in-app navigation (hash route between pillars/subs is the primary nav mechanism per tempo-nav.js) thus fires renderLabel + commitPending. RUNTIME-VERIFY: confirm renderLabel is cheap (label text only) — if it reads BfrbEvents.getAll() it scales with event count on every route.
all.rootCause: Label refresh and pending-commit are wired to broad navigation events; if renderLabel reads the full event store it does an O(events) scan on every hash route.
all.proposedFix: Verify renderLabel does not do an O(n) store scan per route; if it does, cache the count and recompute only on a BFRB log/merge. Debounce commitPending across the 3 events (they can fire together). Low priority pending the runtime check. sw.js CACHE_NAME bump if changed.

all.title: Log Past Session save+cancel handlers wired twice → duplicate sessions + double listeners
all.evidence: js/history-ui.js:73 wires #log-past-save and js/history-ui.js:69 wires #log-past-cancel inside initHistoryPanel(); then initLogPastPanel() wires the SAME #log-past-save at js/history-ui.js:520 and #log-past-cancel at js/history-ui.js:518. Both handlers run on one click.
all.rootCause: Log Past Session logic was duplicated across initHistoryPanel() and initLogPastPanel() during a refactor; the older copy in initHistoryPanel references logModeSelect/logForm/logPastFocusGoals which are scoped INSIDE initLogPastPanel, so that copy also throws a ReferenceError at click time.
all.proposedFix: Delete the duplicated #log-past-save/#log-past-cancel wiring block in initHistoryPanel (js/history-ui.js:69-124) — keep only the initLogPastPanel copy which has the correct closure scope. Verify a single session is written per Save click.

all.title: Space key hijacks contenteditable name/rename edits across modes
all.area: Cross-mode keyboard / Compare, Cards, Pomodoro saved-task rename
all.evidence: All mode keydown handlers guard only INPUT: js/ui.js:32, js/pomodoro-ui.js:161, js/interval-ui.js:42, js/flow-ui.js:348, js/sequence-ui.js:71. Compare names (js/compare-ui.js:106 contenteditable) and instance-card names (js/cards-ui.js:46 contenteditable) and Pomodoro saved-task rename (js/pomodoro-ui.js:919 contenteditable) accept typing while appMode is stopwatch/timer/pomodoro — so pressing Space mid-rename triggers onRightClick/onPomodoroRight (start/stop) AND e.preventDefault() swallows the space character.
all.rootCause: The input-guard predicate checks only e.target.tagName === 'INPUT', missing TEXTAREA and contenteditable elements.
all.proposedFix: Extract a shared isTextEntry(target) helper (target.tagName === 'INPUT' || target.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || target.isContentEditable) mirroring the correct guard already in js/global-bfrb.js:406, and use it in all five mode keydown handlers.

all.title: Destructive actions undoable in Stopwatch but instant & irreversible everywhere else
all.evidence: Stopwatch reset and lap-delete both get a 5s undo toast (js/ui.js:455 showUndoToast, js/ui.js:352 showDeleteUndoToast). But Pomodoro Reset (js/pomodoro-ui.js:247), Pomodoro Finish&Reset (js/pomodoro-ui.js:1491), Flow Reset (js/flow-ui.js:390), Interval Reset (js/interval-ui.js:217), and pomo-clear-all-tasks (js/pomodoro-ui.js:1473 wipes focus+break+actual-work lists) all execute immediately with no confirm and no undo.
all.rootCause: Undo affordance was built per-feature for the stopwatch only; later modes reused the shared btn-left Reset path without an undo layer, and the Actions drawer 'Clear All Tasks' has no guard despite being the most destructive list action.
all.proposedFix: At minimum add a confirm() to pomo-clear-all-tasks and Pomodoro Finish&Reset (they discard user-authored checklists/goals). Ideally generalize the existing undo-toast into a small reusable showUndoToast(label, onUndo) and wire it to Pomodoro/Flow/Interval reset paths so the interaction model is consistent app-wide.

all.title: Tiny tap targets on delete/chip controls — well under 44px
all.area: Cross-cutting (History tags, Pomodoro checklist, Alerts, Interval/Sequence phases, Cards, Presets)
all.evidence: tag-chip-delete is 0.8rem glyph w/ padding 0 2px (css/styles.css:5471); pomo-checklist-item-delete 0.9rem padding 0 4px (css/styles.css:1898); alert-chip-delete 0.9rem padding 0 2px (css/styles.css:1602); interval-phase-del 0.9rem padding 0 4px (css/styles.css:3914); card-delete 1.1rem padding 2px 6px (css/styles.css:992); preset-delete padding 2px 6px (css/styles.css:752). Effective hit area is ~16-24px — far below the 44px iOS/WCAG minimum, on a primarily-phone PWA.
all.rootCause: Delete affordances were styled as inline text glyphs (×) rather than padded touch targets; the swipe-to-delete pattern was only ever applied to stopwatch laps, so list rows elsewhere rely on these undersized × buttons.
all.proposedFix: Give all list-row × delete/chip-delete buttons a min 40-44px touch area (min-width/min-height + larger hit padding, or a transparent ::before expander), keeping the visual glyph small. Apply uniformly via a shared .icon-delete-btn utility class.

all.title: Swipe-to-delete + undo exist only for stopwatch laps; no equivalent for any other list
all.area: Lap list vs all other deletable lists
all.evidence: attachSwipeHandlers (js/ui.js:285) + showDeleteUndoToast (js/ui.js:352) implement swipe-left-to-delete with snap-back, threshold, and undo — only for .lap-swipeable rows. Pomodoro checklist items (js/pomodoro-ui.js:668), flow user-tasks (js/flow-ui.js:775), interval phases, saved tasks, and history tags all delete via a tap-only × with no swipe and no undo.
all.rootCause: The polished gesture was a stopwatch-era feature never generalized; other lists shipped with the minimal × button.
all.proposedFix: Document the intentional inconsistency or, lower-effort, ensure every deletable list at least matches one pattern (tap-× + undo). Full swipe parity is a larger effort; the priority is consistency of the destructive-undo guarantee.

all.title: Flagship offset feature ('start with time elapsed') is a low-contrast text link, easily missed
all.evidence: The differentiating feature is exposed only as <button id='offset-toggle' class='offset-link'>Start with time already elapsed</button> (index.html:337), styled as a muted .offset-link. It sits below the timer with no icon, no example, and is the same visual weight as 'Add alert at time' (index.html:386) and 'Export Laps'. CLAUDE.md calls this the app's key differentiator.
all.rootCause: Secondary controls are all rendered as identical .offset-link text links, so the one high-value, identity-defining action has no visual priority.
all.proposedFix: Elevate the offset entry point: give it an icon + slightly higher contrast, or a one-line example ('e.g. took meds 30 min ago'). Consider surfacing the saved offset presets as quick-pick chips inline when idle, since they're currently buried inside the collapsed panel (js/offset-input.js:143 renderPresetList only renders after the panel opens).

all.title: Compare view is discoverable only via a ⇔ glyph on non-primary cards; no entry point with one instance
all.evidence: enterCompare is reachable only from a .card-compare button (js/cards-ui.js:48, label '⇔') which renders on NON-primary instance cards (js/cards-ui.js:32 skips primary). With a single stopwatch/timer the cards row is empty, so Compare is entirely unreachable until the user discovers 'Add Stopwatch' and creates a second instance. The ⇔ symbol has no text label.
all.rootCause: Compare was wired as a per-card affordance gated behind multi-instance creation, with no top-level discoverability and an icon-only trigger.
all.proposedFix: Add an aria-label/tooltip text to the ⇔ button (currently aria-label='Compare' exists but the glyph alone is opaque) and consider an explicit 'Compare timers' affordance once 2+ instances exist. Document that single-instance users have no path to Compare.

all.title: Sign-in failure is text-only with no retry button; no spinner/disable on the sign-in button during await
all.evidence: Sign-in errors render only as status text 'Sign-in error: <msg>' (js/ui.js... actually js/tempo-nav.js:646-648). The sign-in button is not disabled during the await (js/tempo-nav.js:634), so a slow/timed-out sign-in can be double-tapped. Unlike the hydrate overlay (index.html:34 Retry button), the drawer sign-in error has no inline retry/try-again affordance — the user must find and tap 'Sign in with Google' again.
all.rootCause: The push/reconcile pipelines got in-flight latches + progress UI (renderPushBtn, etc.), but the sign-in click handler was left as a plain async with a catch that only sets status text.
all.proposedFix: Disable signInBtn during the await + show a 'Signing in…' state on the button itself (the status row already shows it), re-enable in finally. Optionally surface a one-tap retry inline with the error.

all.title: No empty/onboarding state for Pomodoro, Flow, or Interval setup screens
all.evidence: Wellness surfaces have rich empty states (meds-empty index.html:818, exercise-recent-empty js/exercise-ui.js:239, wcook-recent-empty). But a first-time Pomodoro user sees only a 25:00 clock + bare 'Focus Goals' list with no items (js/pomodoro-ui.js:610 returns empty innerHTML); Interval setup shows just 'No phases added yet' (index.html:546) with no guidance to tap a template first; Flow shows two duration buttons + an unchecked checklist that silently disables Start (js/flow-ui.js:629 btnRight.disabled) with no explanation of WHY Start is greyed out.
all.rootCause: Onboarding affordances were invested in the newer Wellness pillar but not retrofitted to the original timing modes.
all.proposedFix: Add a one-line hint in each empty setup state (e.g., Interval: 'Pick a template or add phases below'; Flow: when Start is disabled, show 'Complete the checklist or tap Skip to start'). Flow's disabled-Start needs an inline reason most of all.

all.title: Flow Start button silently disabled by unchecked pre-block checklist with no inline reason
all.evidence: canStartFlow() (js/flow-ui.js:499) returns false until every checklist item is checked or 'Skip checklist' is tapped; updateFlowChecklistGate (js/flow-ui.js:922) sets btnRight.disabled = !canStartFlow(). The Start button just appears greyed with no tooltip/message explaining the gate. The Skip link itself hides once all items are checked (js/flow-ui.js:933) which is fine, but a partially-checked state leaves the user with a dead Start button and a Skip link that may scroll out of view.
all.rootCause: The gate is enforced purely via disabled state with no accompanying copy.
all.proposedFix: When Start is disabled in Flow idle, show a short helper line near the button ('Finish the checklist or Skip to begin'). Keep the Skip link adjacent to Start rather than buried in the checklist block.

all.title: Restore-from-backup and Clear-All use native confirm()/alert() — inconsistent with the app's custom modal/toast vocabulary
all.evidence: history-ui.js uses window.confirm for restore (js/history-ui.js:31), window.alert for the result (js/history-ui.js:43), confirm for Clear All (js/history-ui.js:60); meds delete uses confirm (js/meds-ui.js:281). Everywhere else the app uses custom in-DOM affordances (undo-toast, preset delete-confirm inline at js/presets-ui.js:133, Sync.Toast). Native dialogs look foreign on the themed PWA and block the JS thread.
all.rootCause: The destructive-confirm pattern was implemented inconsistently — presets got an inline confirm, but history/meds reached for the browser default.
all.proposedFix: Standardize on one destructive-confirm pattern. The inline-confirm used in presets-ui.js:133 (replace card content with Delete/Cancel) is already in-repo and reusable; route history Clear-All and meds delete through a shared helper. Restore is higher-stakes (wipes IndexedDB) so a modal is justified, but a custom themed one would be more consistent.

all.title: Pomodoro auto-advance 3s countdown is silent to screen readers and has no cancel affordance besides Go-back
all.evidence: startAutoAdvanceCountdown (js/pomodoro-ui.js:193) writes 'Next in 3…' into #auto-advance-overlay (index.html:312) which is a plain div with no aria-live, so the impending phase switch is unannounced. The only way to stop it is the contextually-shown 'Go back' link or pressing the primary button; there's no explicit 'Cancel auto-advance' on the overlay itself.
all.rootCause: The overlay was added as a visual-only countdown without an interaction handle or live-region semantics.
all.proposedFix: Make the auto-advance overlay tappable to cancel (calls cancelAutoAdvance), and give it role='status'/aria-live='polite' so the countdown is announced. The overlay already obscures the timer, so making it the cancel target is natural.

all.title: Rhythm Timeline empty state is a bare sentence with no next-action; readiness band silently vanishes
all.evidence:
Empty timeline renders only '
No entries on this day.
' (js/rhythm-ui.js:263) and status 'Nothing logged yet today.' (js/rhythm-ui.js:252) with no CTA, unlike the Rhythm pillar PLACEHOLDER which does have a 'Start a Flow block' CTA (index.html:936). The readiness band hides entirely when there's no RecoveryFeed row (js/rhythm-ui.js:204) with no 'connect health data' hint, so new users see an empty screen with no explanation of what the pillar offers.
all.rootCause: The timeline empty path predates the richer empty-state conventions and the readiness band has no zero-data placeholder.
all.proposedFix: Add a CTA to the empty timeline (e.g., 'Log a dose or start a focus block to fill your day') and a one-line zero-state for the readiness band rather than fully hiding it on new accounts.

all.title: Primary action feedback inconsistency: Stopwatch animates button text swap, other modes hard-swap innerHTML
all.evidence: Stopwatch uses animateBtn() with an 80ms transition + .btn-transitioning class for label swaps (js/ui.js:160). Every other mode bypasses this and assigns btnRight.innerHTML directly (js/timer-ui.js:159, js/pomodoro-ui.js:452, js/flow-ui.js:624, js/interval-ui.js:350, js/sequence-ui.js:240), so the same physical button animates its Start/Stop label only in stopwatch mode and snaps instantly in all others.
all.rootCause: animateBtn lives inside the UI IIFE and was never extracted for reuse; the other UI modules were written as plain functions that set innerHTML directly.
all.proposedFix: Either accept the inconsistency (low impact) or expose a shared setButtonLabel(btn, text, cls) that all modes call, so the primary button feels identical regardless of mode. Low priority but a visible polish gap.

all.title: Cooking timer mid-nap/in-flight state is lost on tab close; nap timer too — no resume
all.evidence: Nap timer state is purely in-memory: 'no persistence across reloads (if the user closes the tab mid-nap, the timer is gone)' (js/recovery-ui.js:26). Mindful breathing likewise holds state in module vars (js/mindful-ui.js:70-77) and stopBreathing fires on visibilitychange:hidden (js/mindful-ui.js:102), so backgrounding the PWA mid-session silently ends it. This contradicts the app's core drift-free 'survives tab close' promise that Stopwatch/Timer/Pomodoro/Flow all honor.
all.rootCause: Nap and breathing were built as ephemeral UI timers, not engine-backed, so they don't participate in the persistence model the timing modes use.
all.proposedFix: Persist nap startedAt+durationMs to localStorage so a reopened tab can resume or auto-complete (matching the wall-clock model). For breathing, at minimum warn that backgrounding ends the session, or persist enough to resume. Document the intentional gap if resume is out of scope.

all.title: Settings drawer auto-close-on-click can dismiss the drawer mid-interaction for items without data-keep-drawer-open
all.evidence: Every drawer button without [data-keep-drawer-open] auto-closes the drawer 0ms after click (js/tempo-nav.js:310-317). Theme, Sound, Presets, Log-session, Focus all close the drawer — but Theme/Sound open their OWN pickers (#theme-picker, #sound-picker) which are siblings outside the drawer, so the flow is: tap Theme → drawer closes → picker opens elsewhere. The Sound item also has 'Hold for profile' (index.html:87) which on desktop is a contextmenu (js/app.js:376) — a hold/right-click is non-obvious and the meta hint is easy to miss.
all.rootCause: The blanket auto-close was designed for navigation-style items but applies to picker-opening items too, creating a disorienting close-then-open-elsewhere motion.
all.proposedFix: Audit which drawer items should keep the drawer open (pickers that render adjacent) vs close (navigation). Consider rendering Theme/Sound pickers inside the drawer so the interaction stays in one place.

all.title: Stopwatch L/R keyboard shortcuts are undiscoverable and undocumented in-app
all.evidence: js/ui.js:39-44 binds KeyL (lap when running) and KeyR (reset when paused) plus Space; global-bfrb.js:403 binds B. None of these are surfaced anywhere in the UI except Focus mode's hint line (js/focus-ui.js:18). The BFRB FAB title hints 'B' (index.html:1214) but Space/L/R have no affordance, and the shortcut set differs per mode (Pomodoro adds KeyN/Enter at js/pomodoro-ui.js:173, Flow only Space+R) with no consistency or legend.
all.rootCause: Shortcuts accreted per-mode with no central documentation or in-app legend.
all.proposedFix: Add a small keyboard-shortcut legend (e.g., in the settings drawer or a '?' affordance) and reconcile the per-mode shortcut sets so Space=primary, R=reset-when-paused is uniform. Low priority on a touch-first PWA but cheap to document.

all.title: Interval auto-advances phases with zero pause/preview; user cannot rest-gate between phases
all.evidence: On every phase complete the Interval engine immediately advances AND restarts the next phase with no user confirmation (js/interval-ui.js:24-31: advancePhase()+start() fire inside onPhaseComplete). Unlike Pomodoro (which has overflowing/Skip/Break gating) and Sequence, Interval gives no moment to catch breath between work/rest beyond the phase's own duration. For a workout tool this is arguably correct, but it's an interaction-model divergence worth flagging — there's no 'pause between rounds' option.
all.rootCause: Interval was designed as a continuous HIIT runner; the auto-advance is intentional but offers no opt-in gating like the other phase-based modes.
all.proposedFix: Confirm this is intended. If a between-round pause is desired, add an optional 'pause between rounds' toggle mirroring restBetweenRoundsMs. Otherwise document the intentional difference.

all.title: BFRB antecedent-capture popover and if-then plan banner share the bottom-right corner; timing-separated but fragile
all.evidence: On a catch, the capture popover (js/global-bfrb.js:366 showPicker) and the 60s recovery countdown both occupy the bottom-right; the plan banner is deferred until the popover dismisses (js/global-bfrb.js:203 calls BFRBRecovery.showPlan only in commitPending). The separation relies on commitPending being the sole dismiss path; an auto-commit at 30s (AUTO_COMMIT_MS js/global-bfrb.js:61) while the 60s countdown still runs means the plan banner appears 30s into the countdown — a delayed, possibly-confusing reveal. RUNTIME-VERIFY: log a catch, leave the popover open without tapping, confirm the plan banner appears at ~30s and the FAB count is correct.
all.rootCause: Two bottom-corner surfaces were time-multiplexed rather than spatially separated, with the handoff gated on a single code path.
all.proposedFix: Confirm the 30s auto-commit vs 60s countdown overlap is acceptable, or spatially separate the two surfaces so they can coexist. Consider showing the plan banner immediately if no antecedent chips are likely to be tapped.

all.title: Analytics pillar is an empty placeholder requiring a second tap to open the actual dashboard
all.evidence: Tapping the Analytics bottom-tab lands on a placeholder card (index.html:945-963) whose 'Open dashboard' button (inline onclick at index.html:959) clicks a hidden #analytics-toggle (index.html:283) to open the real slide-up panel. So Analytics is a two-tap pillar where every other pillar is one tap to content. The comment at js/tempo-nav.js:184 acknowledges this was deliberate to avoid double-layering, but it's an interaction inconsistency.
all.rootCause: Analytics reuses a pre-Tempo-shell slide-up panel rather than a pillar surface, so the pillar is a launcher rather than the content.
all.proposedFix: Either auto-open the analytics panel when the pillar activates (single tap) or render the dashboard inline in the pillar surface. The current placeholder adds friction to a data view users check often.

all.title: Offset/alert/timer input fields auto-advance on 2 digits but provide no way back; blur silently clamps
all.evidence: Offset fields auto-focus the next field after 2 digits typed (js/offset-input.js:48) and clamp out-of-range silently on blur (js/offset-input.js:54), with only a 400ms border flash for over-max (js/offset-input.js:43 flashBorder). A user typing '5' then pausing gets no advance, but typing '05' jumps away unexpectedly; correcting a mistyped earlier field requires manual back-navigation. Alert fields (js/alert-ui.js) lack even the auto-advance, so the two stopwatch numeric inputs behave differently.
all.rootCause: Auto-advance UX was added to offset inputs only; alert inputs use a plainer handler, and there's no shake/clear feedback beyond a brief border color.
all.proposedFix: Make alert and offset numeric-field behavior consistent (either both auto-advance or neither), and consider a clearer over-max signal than a 400ms border flash.

all.title: Timer/Pomodoro/Flow/Interval/Cooking/Sequence announce no state changes to screen readers
all.area: Timer, Pomodoro, Flow, Interval, Cooking, Sequence modes
all.evidence: js/ui.js:69-75 defines announce() writing to #sr-announce, called ONLY in ui.js (stopwatch: 85,93,107,116). grep across timer-ui.js, pomodoro-ui.js, flow-ui.js, interval-ui.js, sequence-ui.js, cooking-ui.js finds zero announce()/aria-live calls. Timer finish (timer-ui.js:234-236) and Pomodoro phase-complete (pomodoro-ui.js:85-88) only fire SFX.playAlarm()+Platform.notify(). Phase labels (pomodoro-ui.js:380-387) update textContent but are NOT in a live region.
all.rootCause: The shared #sr-announce region + announce() helper were built for the stopwatch-only app and never wired into modes added later; new modes rely on audio + OS notifications, unavailable to SR users.
all.proposedFix: Promote announce() to a shared helper and call it on every visible state transition (timer finished/overflow, pomodoro phase-complete + next-phase, flow focus-complete/recovery, interval phase/round, cooking done, sequence advance). Reuse the assertive #sr-announce region with clear-then-set on RAF as ui.js does.

all.title: Slide-up panels are not dialogs: no focus move, no focus trap, no Escape, no inert background
all.area: History / Analytics / Pomodoro Stats / Presets / Log Past Session panels
all.evidence: index.html:966-996,974-980,293-302,999-1065 are plain divs toggled via .hidden. history-ui.js:7-13 and analytics-ui.js:8-19 just classList.remove/add('hidden') — no element.focus(), no Escape handler, no aria-modal, no role=dialog. Background #app is never inert, so Tab continues into the timer controls behind the open panel.
all.rootCause: Panels were built as CSS slide-up overlays without the dialog interaction contract; focus stays on the trigger button now hidden behind the overlay.
all.proposedFix: Add a small shared modal helper: on open set role=dialog aria-modal + aria-labelledby (existing h3), move focus to close/first focusable, trap Tab, Escape to close, restore focus on close, set siblings inert. ~40 lines vanilla, reused by all five panels + drawer.

all.title: Settings drawer uses invalid role=menu with switches/inputs/sliders as children
all.evidence: index.html:78-79 #tempo-settings-drawer role=menu; children are role=menuitem buttons (80-100) but ALSO role=switch toggles (123,135,161,190), text inputs (175), a range slider (107), role=group sections (101,118,156,185). A menu composite requires only menuitem* children + arrow-key nav, which wireSettingsDrawer (tempo-nav.js:272-323) never implements.
all.rootCause: The drawer was modeled as a menu but evolved into a settings panel with mixed controls; SRs enter menu mode and misreport/skip the switches, inputs, slider.
all.proposedFix: Drop role=menu/menuitem; make it a labelled region or dialog (role=dialog aria-modal + aria-labelledby) with plain buttons. Keep aria-expanded on the toggle.

all.title: Settings drawer + BFRB capture popover don't move focus in on open and don't trap/return focus
all.area: Shell settings drawer; Global BFRB capture popover
all.evidence: tempo-nav.js:281-285 opens drawer by toggling .hidden only — focus stays on gear button; Escape returns focus (297) but click-outside close (286-292) does not. global-bfrb.js:366-371 showPicker() only sets el.hidden=false on the body-appended popover (built 303-333 role=group); no focus moved in, no Escape, click-outside commits but doesn't restore focus. The 'Logged' title (319-320) is not in a live region.
all.rootCause: Both transient surfaces are visual popovers without a focus lifecycle; keyboard users opening the BFRB chips after shortcut B can't reliably reach them.
all.proposedFix: On open move focus to first control (drawer first item; popover first chip/Done). Add Escape-to-close to both. Restore focus to the originating control on close. Fire announce() so the catch is confirmed aurally.

all.title: prefers-reduced-motion almost entirely uncovered; Mindful breathing animation uncontrollable via inline JS transitions
all.area: Mindful breathing; countdown flash; mode switch; BFRB pulse; analog
all.evidence: Only 4 reduced-motion blocks exist (styles.css:3116 hydrate spinner, styles.css:5633 .lap-entering, tempo-shell.css:433 a few nav transitions). NOT covered: mindful-ui.js:150-200 sets runnerCircle.style.transition inline — a media query can't override inline styles and the JS never checks matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion). Also uncovered: mode-fade-in (styles.css:418/421), flash-red 6x alternate (1436,1454,4230), bfrb-pulse scale (2529), bfrb-recovery fill (2553), analog hand transitions.
all.rootCause: Reduced-motion was retrofitted to a few animations, not applied as global policy; the Mindful core animation is created in JS and bypasses CSS.
all.proposedFix: Add a global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block neutralizing transform/opacity animations. For Mindful, gate the inline transition: if matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce).matches set circle scale instantly (transition:none) and rely on the phase-label/phase-count text.

all.title: WCAG AA contrast failures: OLED and Minimal --text-secondary; Minimal link green borderline
all.evidence: Computed: OLED --text-secondary #555555 on #000000 = 2.82:1 (themes.js:46) fails AA; on --btn-bg #0a0a0a = 2.66:1. Minimal --text-secondary #8e8e93 on #ffffff = 3.26:1 (themes.js:37) fails AA. Minimal --green link #007aff on #ffffff = 4.02:1 (themes.js:38) under 4.5:1 for normal .offset-link (styles.css:550-556 0.95rem). --text-secondary is used in 60+ normal-text spots (tab labels tempo-shell.css:304, inactive sub-nav tabs :131, .tempo-settings-item-meta :271-273).
all.rootCause: OLED #555555 chosen for an ultra-dark aesthetic; Minimal reused the dark-theme grey on white. Tokens were never contrast-checked against AA.
all.proposedFix: Bump OLED --text-secondary to >= #8a8a8a (~4.8:1 on #000) and Minimal --text-secondary to >= #6b6b70 (~4.9:1 on #fff). For Minimal links darken --green to #0066d6 (~5.4:1). Verify against bg AND btn-bg per theme.

all.title: Lap deletion is swipe-only with no keyboard/SR-operable alternative
all.evidence: js/ui.js:285-350 attachSwipeHandlers binds only touchstart/touchmove/touchend; deleteLap (339) is reachable solely via a >80px left swipe. The .lap-row markup (ui.js:223-229) renders no delete button and no keyboard handler. Desktop mouse/keyboard and SR users cannot delete a lap.
all.rootCause: Swipe-to-delete was implemented as a touch-only gesture without a parallel accessible control.
all.proposedFix: Render a per-row delete button (aria-label 'Delete lap N', reuse cards-ui.js:49 icon-btn pattern) calling the same deleteLap path, or make rows focusable with Delete/Backspace keydown. Keep swipe as progressive enhancement.

all.title: Sub-44px touch targets: mode-dots (8px), .icon-btn close buttons (~30px)
all.evidence: .mode-dot is 8x8px (styles.css:524-525) — digital/analog switch dots (index.html:324-325) have an 8px hit area, far below 44px (WCAG 2.5.5 / Apple HIG). .icon-btn padding 6px 8px + 1.1rem (styles.css:128-138) ~30px tall, used for all panel close x buttons (index.html:296,969,977,986,1002) + lap mode toggle. .tempo-iconbtn 40x40 (tempo-shell.css:90-91), just under 44.
all.rootCause: Decorative dot styling and compact icon buttons sized for visual density, not pointer ergonomics.
all.proposedFix: Keep the 8px dot visual but expand hit area to >=44px via padding or a ::before / transparent min-width/min-height. Pad .icon-btn and .tempo-iconbtn to 44x44 minimum.

all.title: No document heading structure: zero h1, panels start at h3, Timers/Recovery/Rhythm have no heading
all.evidence: No h1 anywhere in index.html; first heading is the hydrate overlay h2 (line 25). The main Timers screen has no heading. Wellness surfaces jump to h2 (771,838,861,899) with no h1 ancestor. History/Analytics/Stats/Presets/Log-Past panels use h3 (985,968,976,295,1001) with no h2 above. recovery-ui.js:243-266 renders section h3s but no surface h2/h1; rhythm-ui.js:57-68 timeline has no heading. Wordmark uses aria-label on a non-semantic div (index.html:52).
all.rootCause: Headings added per-surface ad hoc; no app-level heading/landmark plan, yielding no rotor outline and inconsistent nesting.
all.proposedFix: Add a visually-hidden h1 per active pillar/mode (.sr-only), normalize panel headings to h1>h2>h3, give Recovery + Rhythm surface headings, wrap primary content in a main landmark with a skip-to-content link as first focusable.

all.title: role=list lap container has non-listitem children
all.evidence: index.html:754 #lap-list role=list; ui.js:206 and 223 render .lap-row as plain div with no role=listitem. An explicit role=list with non-listitem children is reported by SRs as an empty/invalid list, hiding the lap count.
all.rootCause: The container role was added but the row template never got matching item roles.
all.proposedFix: Add role=listitem to each .lap-row (or drop role=list). Optionally aria-label each row 'Lap N, time'.

all.title: user-scalable=no blocks pinch-zoom
all.evidence: index.html:5 meta viewport content includes user-scalable=no, disabling pinch-to-zoom — a WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) violation blocking low-vision users from magnifying any screen.
all.rootCause: user-scalable=no is a common PWA copy-paste to feel app-like and stop double-tap zoom, but removes a core low-vision affordance.
all.proposedFix: Remove user-scalable=no (and any maximum-scale) so viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0. Handle double-tap-zoom with touch-action CSS on specific controls if needed.

all.title: Global BFRB FAB countdown changes meaning but keeps a static aria-label; countdown is silent
all.evidence: index.html:1213-1214 FAB has fixed aria-label 'Log BFRB (shortcut: B)'. bfrb-recovery.js:106 updates btn.textContent to the M:SS countdown 4x/sec (TICK_MS 250 line 15), but the aria-label overrides textContent — SR users never hear the countdown start/progress/completion (SFX.playBFRBEnd line 98 is audio-only). During recovery the button still announces 'Log BFRB' though tapping restarts a catch.
all.rootCause: The FAB doubles as a static action and a live countdown timer, but its accessible name was authored only for the action state and never updated.
all.proposedFix: On recovery start update aria-label (e.g. 'Competing-response timer, N seconds left') or set aria-live on a sibling node; on completion announce 'Reset complete' via announce(). Restore the action aria-label when done.

all.title: Stopwatch keyboard shortcuts are mode-scoped and undiscoverable; other modes lack keyboard parity
all.evidence: ui.js:31-49 binds Space/L/R/Escape but guards if (appMode !== 'stopwatch') return (line 33), so Space-to-start works only in Stopwatch; Timer/Pomodoro/Flow/Interval have no keyboard start/stop (handlers are click-only). No aria-keyshortcuts or visible hint. The global B (global-bfrb.js:402) is the only cross-mode key.
all.rootCause: Keyboard handling was written for the original stopwatch and not generalized when shared btn-left/btn-right handlers gained per-mode guards.
all.proposedFix: Route Space (and Enter on focused controls) through the active mode's primary action, or document that on-screen Start/Stop buttons are canonical (real focusable buttons — a discoverability gap, not a hard block). Add aria-keyshortcuts where shortcuts exist.

all.title: aria-live status rows may be clobbered/silent because the region is hidden when text is set
all.area: Cloud Sync status row; hydrate overlay; BFRB plan banner
all.evidence: #cloud-sync-status (index.html:240-241) is aria-live=polite but starts hidden and tempo-nav.js toggles statusEl.hidden true/false (setStatus 510-523). #bfrb-recovery-plan (index.html:1219) is role=status aria-live=polite shown via hidden=false (bfrb-recovery.js:52). Toggling [hidden] on a live region can suppress announcements in some SRs. RUNTIME-VERIFY: with VoiceOver/NVDA confirm whether sync status, hydrate progress (tempo-nav.js:816-827), and the if-then plan banner are actually announced when revealed.
all.rootCause: Live regions are un-hidden and populated in the same tick; several SR/browser combos only announce mutations to already-rendered visible live regions.
all.proposedFix: Keep live-region containers permanently in the DOM and visible-to-AT (use .sr-only or empty content instead of [hidden]); change only text content. Verify across VoiceOver + NVDA.

all.title: Distraction picker, interval/sequence phase rows, and chips lack labels/state semantics
all.area: Pomodoro/Flow distraction picker; Interval/Sequence run info; BFRB chips
all.evidence: index.html:419-428 #pomo-distraction-picker category buttons have no aria-pressed; the note input (427) has placeholder only, no label/aria-label. interval-ui run-info (#interval-current-phase/#interval-next-phase, index.html:563-565) updates textContent on phase change but is not a live region, so SR users running a HIIT workout get no phase cue. BFRB chips (global-bfrb.js:312-317) toggle .is-selected without aria-pressed.
all.rootCause: Selectable chip/category controls convey state only visually; running-phase displays update silently.
all.proposedFix: Add aria-pressed to toggleable chip/category buttons synced with .is-selected. Give interval/sequence current-phase node aria-live=polite (or announce() on each advance). Add aria-label to unlabeled note inputs.

all.title: Phantom token vocabulary: entire Rhythm pillar references --surface/--text-primary/--accent/--text-muted that are defined nowhere
all.evidence: css/styles.css:5663-5789 + 5999/6048 — .rhythm-nav-btn `background: var(--surface, #2c2c2e)`, .rhythm-day-label `color: var(--text-primary, #f5f5f7)`, .rhythm-now-line `background: var(--accent, #ff453a)`, .rhythm-readiness-band `background: var(--surface, #2c2c2e)`. Counts: --surface x3, --text-primary x4, --accent x10, --text-muted x2. RUNTIME-VERIFY: switch to Ocean/Sunset/Minimal theme and open Rhythm — the timeline chrome stays the dark-mode fallback colors instead of re-theming.

all.proposedFix: Either (a) define the missing tokens in :root + light-mode + each Themes preset, OR (b, lighter) replace the phantom refs with the tokens that DO exist: --surface→--btn-bg, --text-primary→--text, --accent→--red (or a new --now-line token), --text-muted→--text-secondary. Drop the now-dead fallback hex. This makes Rhythm theme correctly across all 6 themes + light mode. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Amber accent #ff9f0a hardcoded 32x as a raw literal despite an unused --orange token; breaks in light mode
all.area: Cross-cutting (BFRB FAB/chips/recovery bar, meds partial/low-supply, cooking cap notice, status-paused, rhythm dots/bars)
all.evidence: Grep `#ff9f0a` = 32 hits across css/styles.css + css/tempo-shell.css (e.g. styles.css:934 .status-paused, 2515/2517 .bfrb-btn, 2583/2584 .global-bfrb-fab, 2769 .bfrb-chip.is-selected, 5827/5837/5856 rhythm bfrb panels; tempo-shell.css:708 .med-status-partial, 873-876 .med-supply-low). So the hardcoded amber never picks up the light-mode #ff9500 and the BFRB/meds amber surfaces stay the dark value on a light background.
all.rootCause: No semantic --amber/--warn token; --orange exists but was bypassed; the BFRB feature shipped its own raw amber literal that propagated by copy-paste.
all.proposedFix: Introduce --amber (and --amber-tint / --amber-dim via color-mix) in :root + light + every theme preset, alias --orange to it, and sweep all 32 #ff9f0a literals (and the rgba(255,159,10,...) variants at tempo-shell.css:873-874 + styles.css:2593) to var(--amber*). One token, ~36 replacements. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: --productivity-accent (blue) is half-wired: drives only the tab indicator; all timer chrome is hardcoded green
all.evidence: tempo-shell.css:12-19 defines --productivity-accent: #007aff and maps --active-accent to it for data-pillar=productivity. But the actual Timers-pillar component CSS in styles.css uses var(--green) / raw green everywhere: .btn-start (855-867), .offset-link (553), .timer-progress-fill (1430), .pomodoro-dot-active (1664), #timer-display.pomodoro-break #time (4226), .pomo-stat-value (1771), .focus-status (4261), cooking-ctrl-start (4185). Grep for --productivity-accent usage outside :root/data-pillar = ZERO. So the productivity pillar's identity blue appears only on the bottom-tab 2px underline (tempo-shell.css:313/325), creating a green-body / blue-tab clash and a dead design token.
all.rootCause: Pillar accent system (tempo-shell.css) was layered on top of the original green-only Stopwatch app without migrating the timer components to consume --active-accent.
all.proposedFix: Decide the intent: either (a) make Timers genuinely blue by swapping var(--green)→var(--active-accent) in the timer-pillar component rules, or (b) if green is the deliberate timing color, set --productivity-accent to the green so the tab indicator matches the body. Pick one to remove the green-body/blue-tab dissonance. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: No spacing scale — 17 distinct integer px values used ad-hoc for gap/padding/margin
all.evidence: Grep of gap/padding/margin px in styles.css yields 17 distinct values: 8(71x),6(51x),4(51x),10(39x),12(36x),2(29x),16(14x),14(9x),20(6x),5(5x),1(4x),40(3x),3(3x),18(3x),60,32,24. The 5px/3px/1px one-offs and the 8↔10↔12↔14↔16 drift mean vertical rhythm is inconsistent between adjacent cards/surfaces (e.g. meds-surface gap:16 vs exercise-surface gap:20 vs mindful-surface gap:22).

all.title: No radius scale — 16 distinct border-radius values (4..26px + 999px)
all.evidence: Grep border-radius px: 10px(36x),8px(35x),12px(24x),14px(13x),6px(7x),4px(7x),2px(6x),3px(3x),18px(3x),5px(2x),16px(2x),999px,7px,26px,24px,11px. The 7px (.med-supply-step:836), 11px, 5px, 26/24px (FAB) one-offs read as accidents next to the dominant 8/10/12/14 family. Pills mix 14px / 16px / 999px for the same chip role (.alert-chip:1583=14 vs .preset-quick-chip:191=16 vs .bfrb-chip:2761=14).
all.rootCause: Each component picked a radius independently; no --radius-* tokens.

all.title: Typography scale is noisy — ~34 distinct rem font-sizes plus 11 px font-sizes mixed in
all.area: Cross-cutting (all CSS; rem app-wide, px leaking in analytics/rhythm)
all.evidence: Grep font-size: 315 rem declarations across 34 distinct values, including visually-indistinguishable neighbors 0.8/0.82/0.84/0.85/0.87/0.88rem and 0.65/0.66/0.68/0.7/0.72/0.74/0.75/0.76/0.78rem.
