Collapse the 0.8x and 0.7x clusters onto two steps; convert the analytics/rhythm px sizes to rem ramp tokens so dashboards respect root font size. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: theme-color meta stays #000000 in Auto/light mode — status bar mismatches a light background
all.evidence: index.html:6 `<meta name="theme-color" content="#000000">`. js/themes.js:72-76 only updates the meta when a preset has explicit vars (`theme.vars ? theme.vars['--bg'] : null`); the 'auto' preset has vars:null (themes.js:5), so when the user is on Auto + the OS is in light mode (styles.css:26-42 sets --bg:#f2f2f7), the meta stays #000000 and the iOS/Android status bar/PWA chrome renders black against the light app. RUNTIME-VERIFY: Auto theme + OS light mode, installed PWA — observe black status bar bleeding into the light UI.
all.rootCause: theme-color is only synced for explicit presets, never for the system-driven Auto path; no prefers-color-scheme listener updates it.
all.proposedFix: In themes.js apply(), when themeId==='auto', set the meta from matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches ? '#f2f2f7' : '#000000' and add a change listener; OR ship two <meta theme-color media="..."> tags (dark/light) in index.html for the Auto baseline. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Big-digit displays use inconsistent font-weight (250/200/300) and two different monospace stacks
all.area: Stopwatch / Pomodoro / Interval / Cooking / Focus time displays
all.evidence: Weights: #time stopwatch font-weight:250 (styles.css:430), pomodoro digit 200 (1139), interval digit 300 (2444), cooking-timer-time 200 (4121), focus-time 200 (4253). Mono stacks: #time uses the long 6-font stack `ui-monospace,'SF Mono',SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Monaco,'Cascadia Mono',monospace` (428) while .lap-time/.card-time/.preset-duration/.interval-phase-dur/.history-dur/.digital-small use a SHORT 4-font stack `ui-monospace,'SF Mono',Menlo,monospace` (e.g. 1324,964,744,3908,5292,505). On a platform missing SF Mono+Menlo, the hero timer and the lap list could resolve to different fallback fonts, and the cross-mode weight drift makes the same role (the primary running clock) look subtly different mode-to-mode.
all.rootCause: Each mode's display was styled independently; no shared --font-mono token or --weight-display token.
all.proposedFix: Define --font-mono (single canonical stack) and --fs-display + a --weight-display in :root; apply to #time, .cooking-timer-time, .focus-time, .interval/.sequence run digits and all secondary mono numerics so the timing typography is one system. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: No elevation system — every box-shadow is a bespoke rgba(0,0,0,...) literal; green/amber glows hardcode the theme color
all.evidence: 15 distinct box-shadows, all literal: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.4) (tempo-settings-drawer 239), 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.25) (FAB 2585 + plan 2663), 0 10px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.3) (bfrb-capture 2724), 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.3)/(.28), 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.3). Glow literals bake the theme color in: rgba(48,209,88,.5) at styles.css:930/1665, rgba(48,209,88,.25) at 2065, rgba(255,159,10,.35) at 2593 — these will NOT track a theme that changes --green/--orange (Ocean green is cyan #0ac7e8, OLED green is #00ff88).
all.rootCause: Shadows authored per-component; glows written as raw rgba instead of color-mix on the accent token.
all.proposedFix: Add --shadow-1/2/3 (and a --shadow-color so light mode can soften) and replace the rgba(0,0,0) shadows. Replace the green/amber glow rgba literals with color-mix(in srgb, var(--green/--amber) N%, transparent) (the codebase already uses this idiom, e.g. styles.css:880, 4448) so glows re-theme. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Phantom motion token --dur-color referenced 6x but defined nowhere; plus an ad-hoc duration grab-bag
all.evidence: tempo-shell.css uses var(--dur-color, 150ms) 6x (lines 98-99, 141-143, 310). Grep `--dur-color:` over css/ = nothing — it always falls back to 150ms, so the token is dead intent. Separately, transition durations across styles.css are an unscaled set: 0.08/0.1/0.12/0.14/0.15/0.18/0.2/0.25/0.3s. Same interaction (button :active) uses 0.08s in some places, 0.1s and 0.12s in others.
all.rootCause: A motion-token system was started (--dur-color) but never landed; durations otherwise picked per-component.
all.proposedFix: Define --dur-fast (120ms), --dur-base (180ms), --dur-slow (300ms), --ease-standard in :root; make --dur-color an alias; snap the 0.08-0.3 grab-bag onto these. Already gated correctly by prefers-reduced-motion (tempo-shell.css:433, styles.css:1357/5633) so no a11y regression. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: No z-index scale — stacking values jump 1→9→10→20→50→100→200→300→1000→2000→2001→9999 with a 9999 typo'd as `z-index:9999`
all.area: Cross-cutting (overlays, drawers, FAB, popovers, focus mode)
all.evidence: Grep z-index: values 0,1,9,10,20,50,100,200,300,1000,2000,2001,9999 — and one un-spaced `z-index:9999` (focus-overlay 4237 area vs another 9999). FAB 2000, bfrb-recovery-plan 2000, bfrb-capture 2001 stack near each other by accident; history/presets/stats panels share 300; analytics 1000; focus 9999. Confirm it does not double-write the hash when the switch already came from a subnav tap (onAppModeChanged early-returns unless activePillar==='timers' and uses replaceState, so it is idempotent). Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: onTimerLeft/onTimerRight duplicate ui.js onLeftClick/onRightClick (documented debt) — and the pattern repeats across all modes

all.title: No shared .card / .empty-state base — 44 *-card and 17 *-empty CSS selectors are bespoke per mode
all.evidence: `grep -ohE '\.[a-z-]*card[a-z0-9-]*' css/*.css | sort -u` → 44 distinct card selectors; `*-empty` → 17. Each surface owns its own family: pomo-stat-card, preset-card, wcook-card, med-card, mindful-pattern-card / mindful-med-card, exercise-card, instance-card (.card-*), cooking-timer-card, recovery-status-card, analytics-card-*. The only shared base classes in CSS are .btn-inner/.btn-start/.btn-stop (styles.css:833-889), .card-* for instance cards, and .modal-backdrop/.modal-subhead (styles.css:3328-3366). No `.card`, `.empty-state`, `.btn-primary`, or `.list-row` base exists.
all.rootCause: Cards were styled per feature as each pillar shipped; no design-token/base-component layer was retrofitted across the Wellness/Rhythm expansion.
all.proposedFix: Introduce a small base layer in tempo-shell.css: `.tempo-card` (padding/radius/shadow/border tokens) and `.tempo-empty` (empty-state layout), then have the bespoke families extend rather than redefine the shared properties (e.g. `.med-card { /* layout-specific only */ }` composed with `.tempo-card`). Do this CSS-first (add base, opt cards in incrementally) to avoid a big-bang. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Active-state class naming inconsistent across components (4 names for one concept)
all.evidence: Four selected/active conventions coexist: mode-tab-active (tempo-nav.js:201, app.js:193 — timers subnav), is-active (tempo-nav.js:204 — wellness/rhythm subnav), is-selected (global-bfrb.js:362,369; recovery-ui.js:405 — chips), and plain 'selected' (6 occurrences). syncSubnavActive (tempo-nav.js:193-206) even branches: timers uses .mode-tab-active 'to preserve legacy JS', others use .is-active.

all.proposedFix: Standardize on one (recommend `.is-active` since it is the newest/most-used in the shell). Keep .mode-tab-active as an alias selector in CSS during migration so legacy JS that introspects it (tempo-nav.js:234 currentAppMode reads .mode-tab.mode-tab-active) keeps working. Document the convention in CLAUDE.md Conventions. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Three independent toast systems with no shared primitive
all.evidence: ui.js has TWO near-identical builders: showUndoToast (ui.js:455-475) and showDeleteUndoToast (ui.js:352-372) — both createElement('div') with .undo-toast, an inline `<button class="undo-btn">Undo</button>`, requestAnimationFrame reveal, and a 5s setTimeout dismiss. all.title: Relative-time / 'today'/'yesterday'/'ago' humanizers reimplemented in 5 files

all.title: Dead code in app.js: originalOnLeftClick assigned-never-read + empty no-op listener

The immediately-following app.js:482-484 adds a click listener whose entire body is `if (appMode !== 'stopwatch') return;` — a no-op. The comment above (app.js:480) says 'Hook into stopwatch reset to save history' but the actual save logic lives in the setInterval at app.js:489-512, making the listener vestigial.

all.title: 'Timer Complete' / 'Your countdown has finished!' notification copy triplicated
all.evidence: The same title+body literal appears at timer-ui.js:93 (BgNotify.schedule), timer-ui.js:236 (Platform.notify), and app.js:282 (reschedule BgNotify.schedule). Any copy change must be made in 3 places.

all.title: Visibility-toggle idiom split three ways (classList 'hidden' vs el.hidden vs data-collapsed)
all.evidence: Three competing show/hide conventions: classList.toggle('hidden') ~147 occurrences (app.js applyAppMode:202-227 alone toggles ~24 elements this way), el.hidden = boolean ~65 occurrences (tempo-nav.js wellness sub showWellnessSub:208-212, cloud-sync rows), and data-collapsed attribute ~16 (timer-ui.js:11-32 offset/set inputs, per CLAUDE.md note for CSS max-height transitions). Mixing .hidden class with the hidden attribute is a known footgun (a .hidden{display:none} rule can fight `el.hidden`).

RUNTIME-VERIFY there is no element that receives both a .hidden CSS rule and el.hidden=false (would render hidden unexpectedly). Mechanical, low-value; bundle with the CSS base-class work. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME if any markup changes.

all.title: Two cooking surfaces (Timers>Cook and Wellness>Cooking) — distinct routes/engines for overlapping intent
all.evidence: Timers subnav has data-app-mode='cooking' data-subnav-key='cook' (index.html:265) routing to the Cook timing mode (cooking-ui.js). Wellness subnav has data-subnav-key='cooking' (index.html:271) → data-wellness-sub='cooking' (index.html:891) routing to wellness-cooking-ui.js (8 named presets → createTimer). Routing is technically correct (cook vs cooking are different keys) but two near-identical 'cooking timers' destinations is an IA discoverability/consistency smell — users may not know which to use, and the two share no code.

all.proposedFix: Product/IA decision (taste-level): either (a) make Wellness>Cooking a preset launcher that hands off INTO Timers>Cook (single engine surface), or (b) clearly differentiate copy/labels so the split is intentional. No code change proposed without a product call; flagging for the synthesis gate.

all.title: Backup omits the bfrb_events store — all post-migration BFRB catches are silently lost on export/restore
all.evidence: js/export.js:74-130 EXPORT_SETTINGS_KEYS lists only legacy BFRB keys ('pomodoro_bfrbs' L84, 'flow_bfrbs' L93, 'bfrbs_global' L118) — never 'bfrb_events'. js/bfrb-events.js:51 STORAGE_KEY='bfrb_events' is the F3 single source of truth; js/bfrb-events.js:157-264 _runMigration writes consolidated data to bfrb_events and sets a marker but never deletes the legacy keys. Confirmed: `grep bfrb_events js/export.js js/backup.js` returns nothing. So every catch logged AFTER the one-time migration goes only to bfrb_events and is excluded from buildBackupData() — and backup.js reuses Export.buildBackupData for the F12 mandatory pre-push backup.
all.rootCause: EXPORT_SETTINGS_KEYS is a hand-maintained list that was never updated when F3 consolidated the three legacy BFRB arrays into the single bfrb_events store; the migration keeps the now-empty legacy keys, masking the omission for old data.
all.proposedFix: Add 'bfrb_events' to EXPORT_SETTINGS_KEYS so buildBackupData captures it, and have importAllData restore it like any other settings key. Keep the legacy keys for pre-migration backups. Add a test in the export suite asserting 'bfrb_events' is in getSettingsKeys(). Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Analytics dashboard uses Promise.all with no error isolation — one corrupt query bricks the entire panel forever
all.evidence: js/analytics-ui.js:623-641 renderAnalytics() sets content to 'Loading...' then awaits Promise.all([...12 Analytics.getX() calls...]) with no try/catch. If ANY single query rejects (corrupt IndexedDB session, a malformed record in History/bfrb_events/distractions), the whole await rejects, html is never built, content.innerHTML stays 'Loading...' permanently with an unhandled rejection. RhythmInsights deliberately uses Promise.allSettled for per-panel isolation (CLAUDE.md note on rhythm-insights.js) — Analytics never got the same treatment.
all.rootCause: Promise.all is fail-fast and there is no surrounding try/catch or per-card fallback; the all-or-nothing render assumes every analytics query always resolves.
all.proposedFix: Switch to Promise.allSettled and render each card from its settled value (use a safe default on 'rejected'), or wrap the block in try/catch and show an inline error/retry state instead of an eternal spinner. Mirror the allSettled pattern already in rhythm-insights.js. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Meds 'Took it now' / 'apply offset' dose logging has no double-tap debounce — double-counts a safety-relevant medication
all.evidence: js/meds-ui.js:215-221 (action==='log-now') calls med.logDose(); MedsManager.saveAll() immediately, and js/meds-ui.js:236-247 (apply-offset) the same — neither has a debounce/lock. Pomodoro deliberately has a click-debounce lock (CLAUDE.md: 'Pomodoro also has a click debounce lock'), but dose logging — which feeds adherence stats AND derived prescription-supply remaining (js/meds.js:94-102) — has none. A fast double-tap logs two doses, double-decrementing the supply badge and double-counting adherence.
all.rootCause: No debounce/disable-after-click guard on the dose-log buttons; the card click handler fires synchronously on every tap.
all.proposedFix: Add a short (~600ms) per-card debounce lock around log-now / apply-offset (same shape as the Pomodoro lock), or disable the button briefly after a successful logDose. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Focus/Ambient full-screen overlay is invisible to screen readers and has no focus management
all.evidence: js/focus-ui.js:12-20 builds overlay as a bare <div id='focus-overlay'> with inner time/status/hint divs — no role, no aria-label/aria-modal, no tabindex, no aria-live on #focus-time. enter() (L8-59) never moves focus into the overlay and never traps it; exit (L61-79) never restores focus. Tap/double-tap drive pause/lap via pointer only (L25-42); the sole keyboard affordance is Escape (L129-131) — no keyboard pause/lap. The a11y lens covered slide-up .hidden panels and the settings drawer but NOT this full-screen overlay, which is a separate surface created/destroyed at runtime.
all.rootCause: Focus mode was built as a pointer-first ambient display; ARIA semantics and keyboard/focus management were never added to the dynamically-created overlay.
all.proposedFix: Add role='dialog' aria-modal='true' aria-label='Focus display', aria-live='polite' on the time element, move focus to the overlay on enter and restore on exit, mark the background inert (or aria-hidden) while active, and add keyboard handlers for pause/resume + lap alongside Escape. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Focus/Ambient mode controls only stopwatch/timer/pomodoro — interval is display-only and flow is unsupported
all.evidence: js/focus-ui.js:139-145 getTimeMs() handles stopwatch, timer, pomodoro, AND interval (L143) — but handleTap() (L83-127) only pauses/resumes stopwatch (L99), timer (L108), pomodoro (L116); there is no interval branch. So in interval mode Focus shows a live countdown but tapping does nothing. getTimeMs returns 0 for flow/cooking/sequence, so Focus shows 00:00 if entered from those modes. getStatusText() (L147-162) also only knows stopwatch/timer/pomodoro.
all.rootCause: Focus mode's tap handler and status mapping were written for the original three modes and never extended when interval/flow were added, despite getTimeMs gaining an interval branch.
all.proposedFix: Either add interval/flow control branches to handleTap()+getStatusText() for parity, or gate the focus-toggle button so Focus is only offered in modes it fully supports. Lowest-risk: hide/disable focus-toggle outside the supported modes and add the interval pause branch. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: switchAppMode never updates the URL hash — direct mode switches desync the route and break deep-link/back
all.evidence: js/app.js:162-183 switchAppMode() sets appMode + localStorage('app_mode') + applyAppMode() but never writes the hash and never calls TempoNav. js/tempo-nav.js:1202-1208 onAppModeChanged is exported but (per IA lens, confirmed) never called. So any mode change NOT routed through TempoNav.applyRoute (e.g. legacy .mode-tab clicks via app.js:156, or programmatic switchAppMode) leaves window.location.hash stale; a subsequent reload or shared URL restores the wrong mode, and the back button is inconsistent.
all.rootCause: Two parallel mode-entry paths (TempoNav.applyRoute writes the hash; app.js switchAppMode does not) with the bridging hook (onAppModeChanged) wired but never invoked.
all.proposedFix: Have switchAppMode call TempoNav.onAppModeChanged(mode) (which should writeHash for MODE_TO_SUB[mode]) after it commits, or route all mode tab clicks through TempoNav.applyRoute. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: No <noscript> fallback and no first-paint message — JS failure shows a blank/broken shell
all.evidence: `grep -in noscript index.html` returns nothing. The entire UI is rendered by ~80 serial <script> tags (CLAUDE.md) with no defer/async; if any early module 404s or throws, or JS is disabled, the user sees an empty app shell with no explanation. The performance lens flagged the render-blocking script tags but not the absence of any graceful no-JS / load-failure fallback.
all.rootCause: Vanilla no-build app assumed JS is always present and all scripts always load; no defensive fallback was added.
all.proposedFix: Add a <noscript> block with a short 'JavaScript is required' message inside #app, and optionally a minimal inline first-paint placeholder. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: No body-scroll-lock behind any overlay — settings drawer, slide-up panels, BFRB popover, and Focus overlay let the page scroll underneath
all.evidence: `grep body.style.overflow|no-scroll|scroll-lock js/*.js` finds no scroll-lock anywhere (only an unrelated CSS overflow:hidden comment in rhythm-panel-focus-minutes.js:56). The settings drawer (tempo-nav.js), slide-up panels (history/analytics/etc.), the BFRB capture popover (global-bfrb.js:303+), and the full-screen Focus overlay (focus-ui.js:12-20) all appear without locking <body> scroll, so background content scrolls behind them on touch — a known mobile-overlay UX defect the a11y lens (focus-trap) and ux lens did not call out.
all.rootCause: Overlays are .hidden/append-to-body toggles with no shared open/close lifecycle that locks background scroll.
all.proposedFix: Introduce a tiny shared helper (lock/unlock body scroll by toggling a CSS class that sets overflow:hidden + position:fixed top:-scrollY) and call it from each overlay's open/close. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

all.title: Nine always-live global keydown listeners, one per mode, none ever removed — every keypress fans out to all of them
all.evidence: `grep document.addEventListener('keydown' js/*.js` = 9 registrations: ui.js:31, timer? (via flow-ui.js, interval-ui.js, pomodoro-ui.js, sequence-ui.js:69), focus-ui.js:45, global-bfrb.js:402, todoist-ui.js, tempo-nav.js. Each is added once at init and never removed; each immediately bails on an appMode guard, but all 9 still execute on every keystroke for the app's lifetime. This is the IA lens 'duplicated state machine' theme but from the global-listener-leak angle, which no lens owns. Note ui.js:32 also guards only tagName==='INPUT' (not TEXTAREA / isContentEditable), so Space is preventDefault'd over contenteditable instance names in stopwatch mode (cards-ui.js uses contenteditable).
all.rootCause: Each mode UI module independently attaches its own document-level keydown handler at init rather than a single shared dispatcher that routes by appMode.
all.proposedFix: Consolidate into one shared document keydown dispatcher that switches on appMode and delegates to the active mode (companion to unifying the btn-left/btn-right state machine), and broaden the input guard to include TEXTAREA + isContentEditable. Bump sw.js CACHE_NAME.

designDirections.name: Refined Minimal (recommended) — consolidate, don't redecorate
designDirections.philosophy: Keep the current restrained iOS-stopwatch character but fix the system underneath it: one coherent token layer, one accent per pillar, generous whitespace, ultra-quiet chrome. The product already wants to be calm; this just makes it consistent. Lowest taste risk because the visual language barely changes — only the inconsistencies disappear.
designDirections.tokens: Type ramp: --fs-xs .68 / -sm .8 / -base .9 / -md 1 / -lg 1.25 / -xl 1.5rem + --fs-display clamp(3.2rem,14vw,5.5rem); all display digits weight 250, single --font-mono stack. Color: rename --green→--accent-primary (success stays the green hue), keep pillar accents but RESOLVE the green/blue clash by setting --productivity-accent to the timing green so body+tab agree; add --amber + --danger + --surface tokens and wire themes.js to set them all. designDirections.philosophy: Lean into the wellness/focus identity: a warmer dark base, lower overall contrast for long focus sessions, and the running clock as the single dominant element on every timing screen. Pillars distinguished by a soft tint wash on surfaces rather than a saturated accent, reducing the current green/blue/amber color noise.

Accent: a single warm amber-gold --accent #f5a623 used sparingly; pillars expressed as --surface-tint (productivity cool-tint, wellness green-tint, rhythm neutral) applied at ~6% on cards, NOT as button colors. designDirections.philosophy: Treat Tempo as a quantified-self instrument. Timing screens stay clean, but the Rhythm/Analytics/insights pillars get a denser, higher-contrast, chart-forward grid with crisp tabular numerals and a real categorical data palette — turning the 9 insight panels from afterthoughts into the centerpiece.

Type: tighter dashboard ramp with px→rem ramp tokens so panels finally scale; numerals weight 600 tabular, labels 0.66rem uppercase --track-label 0.06em. Layout: 2-up card grid on >=520px for insight panels, denser --space-2/3 padding, --radius-md cards, hairline 0.5px --separator dividers, sparkline stroke 1.5. Higher-contrast --text on slightly elevated --surface. Motion minimal (data shouldn't bounce): --dur-fast only, bars grow on enter once.

Con: most scoped effort and concentrated in the data pillars; denser UI can feel busy on phones (needs careful responsive collapse); contrast bump and 2-up grid need runtime layout verification on narrow screens.

lensSummaries.summary: The timing engines are well-built: the drift-free wall-clock model is consistent across Stopwatch/Timer/Pomodoro/Flow/Interval/Sequence, every loadState has a future-clock-skew guard and a missed-completion recovery path, and the overshoot state machine is carefully reasoned. The highest-impact correctness defects are in the UI/persistence seams rather than the engines: (1) Cooking timers persist their non-overshoot Timer state but the loadState recovery never re-fires the alarm callback that logs history AND the auto-commit/alarm wiring binds a stale array index, (2) a stale 'focusComplete' status string survives in app.js:217 that the engine renamed to 'overflowing', leaving a progress-bar visibility branch dead, (3) Cooking timers that finish while the tab is closed silently lose their History session because the alarm-driven addSession only fires from the live RAF loop, mirroring a gap Flow explicitly patches but Cooking, Interval, Sequence, and Timer do not, and (4) several rapid-double-click and missed-completion edges. Engine internals are sound; the bugs cluster at restore-time and the shared-button/RAF boundary. Most fixes are small and low-risk; none require touching the frozen sync layer or the drift-free model.

The single most impactful class of perf problem is per-RAF-frame full-DOM rebuilds in the countdown modes. Stopwatch's render loop is well-architected (it only touches the current-lap text node via updateCurrentLap), but Pomodoro, Flow, Timer, and Interval all call their entire updateXxxUI() function on every animation frame (~60fps), and several of those functions do innerHTML rebuilds, classList toggles, and even synchronous localStorage reads + JSON.parse every frame. Pomodoro is the worst: renderPomodoroDots() and renderPomodoroTimeline() both do full innerHTML rebuilds — and the timeline rebuild reads localStorage + parses JSON + calls toLocaleTimeString — ~60 times/second for the entire session. Secondary issues: an always-on 500ms setInterval in app.js that runs for the whole app lifetime regardless of mode, several setInterval tickers that are started but never stopped (meds-ui 30s ticker, the app.js poller) plus a Map that grows without eviction, the renderLaps full-innerHTML rebuild on each lap event (confirmed, the CLAUDE.md-noted issue), and 80 render-blocking serial <script> tags with no defer/async hurting TTI. The drift-free timing model itself is correct and should be hardened, not rewritten.

Tempo's interaction model is broadly coherent — a shared btn-left/btn-right state machine with per-mode guards, RAF-driven displays, and undo toasts for the two destructive stopwatch actions (reset, lap-delete). But the UX consistency breaks down across modes in ways a real user feels: destructive actions are undoable in Stopwatch yet instant-and-silent everywhere else (Pomodoro Reset/Finish, Flow Reset, clear-all-tasks, preset/timer/meds deletes), swipe-to-delete and undo exist only for stopwatch laps, and the discoverability of the app's flagship offset feature plus Compare/Presets is weak. The biggest correctness-adjacent UX bugs: history-ui.js double-wires the Log Past Session save/cancel handlers (duplicate sessions + double event-handler attach), and every mode's keyboard handler guards only INPUT — so Space hijacks contenteditable name/rename edits and the BFRB plan textarea path. Tap targets for the dense delete/chip controls (tag delete, checklist delete, alert/interval phase delete, card delete) are 0.8–1.1rem glyphs with 0–6px padding, far under the 44px minimum, making one-handed phone deletes error-prone. Empty/onboarding states are strong in Wellness (Meds/Exercise/Cooking) but absent in Pomodoro/Flow/Interval setup and the Rhythm timeline, and sign-in/sync error UX is text-only with no retry affordance outside the boot overlay.

Tempo has a thin a11y veneer (one #sr-announce live region + :focus-visible outlines) but coverage is shallow and inconsistent across the large surface. Biggest systemic gaps: only Stopwatch announces state/lap changes — Timer, Pomodoro, Flow, Interval, Cooking, Sequence, the BFRB countdown, and meds/recovery are silent to screen readers, relying on sound + OS notifications; every slide-up panel and the settings drawer is a non-modal .hidden toggle with no focus-move-on-open, no focus trap, no Escape (except the drawer), no inert/aria-modal; prefers-reduced-motion covers only 3 trivial things and the Mindful breathing circle uses inline JS transitions the media query can't reach; OLED and Minimal themes have concrete WCAG AA contrast failures (text-secondary 2.82:1 / 3.26:1). Plus 8px touch targets, swipe-only lap deletion with no keyboard path, no h1/landmark structure, an invalid role=menu drawer, and user-scalable=no blocking pinch-zoom.

Tempo's timing core is solid on the one thing that matters most for a stopwatch — tabular numerals are applied consistently (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on ~55 selectors incl. all time displays), so digits do not jitter. Below that, the design system has eroded badly through accretion: there is no shared token scale for spacing, radius, type, motion, z-index, or elevation, and three parallel color vocabularies coexist. (1) The legacy iOS palette (--green/--red/--btn-bg in styles.css :root), (2) the Tempo pillar palette (--active-accent etc. in tempo-shell.css), and (3) an entirely PHANTOM Rhythm vocabulary (--surface, --text-primary, --accent, --text-muted) that is defined NOWHERE and only ever resolves to hardcoded fallback hex — so the whole Rhythm pillar ignores the theme system and never re-themes for Ocean/Sunset/Minimal/OLED. The amber accent (#ff9f0a) is duplicated as a raw literal 32 times despite an unused --orange token existing, and won't adapt to light mode. The defined --productivity-accent (blue) is half-wired: it drives only the tab indicator while all actual timer chrome stays hardcoded green, so the productivity pillar's identity color is essentially dead. Recommended fix is token-first: ratify a single :root token layer (semantic color incl. --amber/--warn and --danger, a 4px spacing scale, a radius scale, a type ramp, a duration scale, z-index layers, and elevation shadows), wire the phantom Rhythm tokens to it, then sweep literals per-screen. Three design directions follow.

Tempo's PWA shell is competently built (cache-first SW with version cleanup, a real native seam in platform.js, well-considered bottom safe-area math), but the platform layer has one silent foundational defect and several reliability/install gaps. The biggest issue: the viewport meta lacks `viewport-fit=cover`, which makes every `env(safe-area-inset-*)` value resolve to 0 on iOS standalone — silently neutralizing all the safe-area work already written in both CSS files, and combined with a `black-translucent` status bar means the sticky top bar draws under the notch. There is no Wake Lock anywhere, so the screen sleeps mid-timing (a stopwatch/Pomodoro/Flow app's core use case) and the in-page Web Audio alarm + RAF loop die when the screen locks. The SW has no update-to-reload UX (open tabs run stale code indefinitely — the documented stale-cache pain), and there's no iOS install affordance (iOS never fires beforeinstallprompt). Smaller correctness issues: BgNotify silently no-ops on the very first session before the SW controls the page, the theme-color meta goes stale on the 'auto' theme, AudioContext is never resumed, and the manifest ships a "(feature branch)" description plus is missing id/scope/maskable-icon/orientation.

Tempo's information architecture shows a clean shell (tempo-nav.js routing, shared Utils.formatMs/formatShort, a single shared escapeHtml in dom-utils.js, Platform.haptic/notify as the only native seam — no direct navigator.vibrate or new Notification anywhere outside platform.js) but significant copy-paste drift at the module layer. The biggest IA debt is that all six timing modes (stopwatch/ui.js, timer, pomodoro, flow, interval, cooking, plus sequence) independently re-implement the same btn-left/btn-right state machine — each registers its own listener on the two shared button elements, hand-rolls the idle/running/paused/finished switch with copy-pasted `<span class="btn-inner">` innerHTML, and gates on `appMode !== 'x'` (65 such guards). Component patterns are fragmented: 44 distinct `*-card` CSS selectors and 17 `*-empty` selectors with no shared `.card`/`.empty-state` base, four different active-state class names (mode-tab-active / is-active / is-selected / selected), feature-prefixed primary/secondary buttons with no shared `.btn-primary`, and three separate toast systems. Shared helpers exist but are bypassed: escapeHtml is re-defined locally in 4 files, formatDuration in 3, and date-key/relative-time logic ("today"/"ago") is hand-rolled in 5+ files despite Utils.localDateKey existing. There is also dead/never-wired routing code (TempoNav.onAppModeChanged is exported but never called, so hash drifts out of sync on non-nav mode switches; app.js:481 originalOnLeftClick is assigned-never-read with an empty no-op listener).

The seven lenses covered the timing engines, render loops, design tokens, a11y of panels, and the PWA shell well, but several whole surfaces and cross-cutting resilience seams slipped through. The biggest gap is a confirmed DATA-LOSS bug: the F3 consolidated `bfrb_events` store — the single source of truth for every BFRB catch — is entirely absent from EXPORT_SETTINGS_KEYS, so backup/restore silently drops all post-migration catches (the legacy keys it does list are stale after migration). Other under-owned issues: the full-screen Focus/Ambient overlay has zero a11y and inconsistent mode coverage (interval shows but can't be controlled, flow unsupported); the Analytics dashboard uses Promise.all with no per-query isolation so one corrupt session bricks the whole panel into a permanent "Loading…"; meds dose-logging has no double-tap debounce (double-counts a safety-relevant med); switchAppMode never syncs the URL hash; and there is no <noscript> fallback, no body-scroll-lock on any overlay, and 9 always-live global keydown listeners. None require touching the frozen sync layer or the drift-free model.
